sentences.greek: ὁ κῆρυξ τῇ τετάρτῃ νυκτὶ ἀφίκετο.

sentences.smooth_english: The herald arrived on the fourth night.

sentences.greek: ἡ πόλις αὐτὴ διεφθάρη ὑπὸ τῶν πολεμίων.
sentences.literal_english: The city itself was destroyed by the enemy.
sentences.smooth_english: The city itself was destroyed by the enemy.

sentences.greek: πέντε ἡμερῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀφιξόμεθα.
sentences.literal_english: We shall arrive at the city in five days.
sentences.smooth_english: We shall arrive at the city in five days.

sentences.greek: διέφθειρε πάσας τὰς τῶν Ἀθηναίων ναῦς.
sentences.literal_english: He destroyed all the ships of the Athenians.
sentences.smooth_english: He destroyed all the ships of the Athenians.

sentences.greek: μὴ διαφθείρωμεν τὰ τῆς πόλεως τείχη.
sentences.literal_english: Let us not destroy the walls of the city.
sentences.smooth_english: Let us not destroy the walls of the city.

sentences.greek: πολλὰ δῶρα πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἐπέμφθη ὑπὸ τοῦ αὐτοῦ ἀνδρός.
sentences.literal_english: Many gifts were sent to us by the same man.
sentences.smooth_english: Many gifts were sent to us by the same man.

sentences.greek: αἱ νῆες τῇ αὐτῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἀφικνοῦνται εἰς τὸν λιμένα.
sentences.literal_english: The ships arrive in the harbour on the same day.
sentences.smooth_english: The ships arrive in the harbour on the same day.

sentences.greek: οἱ πολέμιοι διέφθειραν τὰ μεγάλα τείχη.
sentences.literal_english: The enemy destroyed the great walls.
sentences.smooth_english: The enemy destroyed the great walls.

sentences.greek: τεττάρων μηνῶν ἀφίξονται εἰς τὴν αὐτὴν πόλιν.
sentences.literal_english: They will arrive at the same city in four months.
sentences.smooth_english: They will arrive at the same city in four months.

sentences.greek: πάντα διεφθάρη ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστάντων.
sentences.literal_english: Everything was destroyed by those who had revolted.
sentences.smooth_english: Everything was destroyed by those who had revolted.

sentences.greek: εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀφικόμενος ἤγγειλε τὴν νίκην.
sentences.literal_english: Having arrived at the city, he announced the victory.
sentences.smooth_english: Having arrived at the city, he announced the victory.

sentences.greek: οὗτος ὁ στρατηγὸς οὐ νικήσει τὸν τῶν Περσῶν βασιλέα.
sentences.literal_english: This general will not conquer the king of the Persians.
sentences.smooth_english: This general will not conquer the king of the Persians.

sentences.greek: οὐκ ἤθελον πείθεσθαι τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἡγεμόσιν.
sentences.literal_english: They were not willing to obey the same leaders.
sentences.smooth_english: They were not willing to obey the same leaders.

sentences.greek: οἱ φύλακες αὐτοὶ ἀπέθανον ὑπὸ τῶν πολεμίων.
sentences.literal_english: The guards themselves were killed by the enemy.
sentences.smooth_english: The guards themselves were killed by the enemy.

sentences.greek: ὁ Σωκράτης οὐ διέφθειρε τοὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει νεανίας.
sentences.literal_english: Socrates did not corrupt the young men in the city.
sentences.smooth_english: Socrates did not corrupt the young men in the city.

sentences.greek: μὴ διαφθείρητε τὰ τῆς πόλεως τείχη, ὦ Ἀθηναῖοι.
sentences.literal_english: Do not destroy the walls of your city, Athenians.
sentences.smooth_english: Do not destroy the walls of your city, Athenians.

sentences.greek: ὁ Δημοσθένης αὐτὸς ἔπεισεν αὐτοὺς πορεύεσθαι.
sentences.literal_english: Demosthenes himself persuaded them to march.
sentences.smooth_english: Demosthenes himself persuaded them to march.

sentences.greek: οἱ αὐτοὶ στρατιῶται νυκτὸς προσέβαλον (ἐπέθεντο) τῇ πόλει.
sentences.literal_english: The same soldiers attacked the city by night.
sentences.smooth_english: The same soldiers attacked the city by night.

sentences.greek: ὁ βασιλεὺς αὐτὸς οὐ πολὺ ἀπεῖχε τῶν ἱππέων.
sentences.literal_english: The king himself was not far distant from the cavalry.
sentences.smooth_english: The king himself was not far distant from the cavalry.

sentences.greek: μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ὁ στρατηγὸς ἀφίκετο μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς στρατιᾶς.
sentences.literal_english: After three days the general arrived with the same army.
sentences.smooth_english: After three days the general arrived with the same army.

sentences.greek: οἱ πολλὰ γράφοντες οὐκ ἀεὶ ποιηταὶ γίγνονται.
sentences.literal_english: Those who write many things do not always become poets.
sentences.smooth_english: Those who write many things do not always become poets.

sentences.greek: τὴν πόλιν διαφθείρας ἐβουλήθη πάντας τοὺς πολίτας ἀποκτείνειν.
sentences.literal_english: Having destroyed the city, he wished to kill all the citizens.
sentences.smooth_english: Having destroyed the city, he wished to kill all the citizens.

sentences.greek: εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα ἀφικόμενος ἐβουλήθη εἰς τὰ ὄρη ἐλθεῖν.
sentences.literal_english: Having arrived in Greece, he wished to go to the mountains.
sentences.smooth_english: Having arrived in Greece, he wished to go to the mountains.

sentences.greek: ὁ αὐτὸς ἀνὴρ προὔδωκε τὴν πόλιν τοῖς πολεμίοις.
sentences.literal_english: The same man betrayed the city to the enemy.
sentences.smooth_english: The same man betrayed the city to the enemy.

sentences.greek: πρὸς τὴν νῆσον ἐλθὼν κήρυκα ἀπέπεμψεν.
sentences.literal_english: Having come to the island, he despatched a herald.
sentences.smooth_english: Having come to the island, he despatched a herald.

sentences.greek: ἡ ἡμετέρα πόλις οὐ δέξεται τοὺς σοὺς νόμους.
sentences.literal_english: Our city will not receive your laws.
sentences.smooth_english: Our city will not receive your laws.

sentences.greek: ἡ αὐτὴ γυνὴ τοῦθ’ ἡμῖν εἶπεν.
sentences.literal_english: The same woman told us this.
sentences.smooth_english: The same woman told us this.

sentences.greek: αὐτοὶ οὐκ ἀεὶ τὰ αὐτὰ θαυμάζομεν.
sentences.literal_english: We ourselves do not all admire the same things.
sentences.smooth_english: We ourselves do not all admire the same things.

sentences.greek: οἱ εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀφικόμενοι τὰ αὐτὰ ἤγγειλαν.
sentences.literal_english: Those who arrived at the city announced the same things.
sentences.smooth_english: Those who arrived at the city announced the same things.

sentences.greek: πάντες ὑπὸ τοῦ αὐτοῦ ῥήτορος ἐψεύσθημεν.
sentences.literal_english: We were all deceived by the same orator.
sentences.smooth_english: We were all deceived by the same orator.

sentences.greek: τῇ τετάρτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τὴν πόλιν ἐλάβομεν.
sentences.literal_english: We took the city on the fourth day.
sentences.smooth_english: We took the city on the fourth day.

sentences.greek: αὐτὸν τὸν βασιλέα οὐκ ὀψόμεθα.
sentences.literal_english: We shall not see the king himself.
sentences.smooth_english: We shall not see the king himself.

sentences.greek: τὴν αὐτὴν γυναῖκα εἶδον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
sentences.literal_english: They saw the same woman in the road.
sentences.smooth_english: They saw the same woman in the road.

sentences.greek: πολλὰ καὶ καλὰ δένδρα ὁρῶμεν ἐν τῇ νήσῳ.
sentences.literal_english: We see many beautiful trees in the island.
sentences.smooth_english: We see many beautiful trees in the island.

sentences.greek: τριῶν ἡμερῶν ληψόμεθα τὴν πόλιν.
sentences.literal_english: We shall take the city in three days.
sentences.smooth_english: We shall take the city in three days.

sentences.greek: εἰς τὸν νεὼν ἀφικόμενος τὸν αὐτὸν ἱερέα εἶδεν.
sentences.literal_english: Having arrived at the temple he saw the same priest.
sentences.smooth_english: Having arrived at the temple he saw the same priest.

sentences.greek: οἱ ἀγαθοὶ κριταὶ οὐ δῶρα λαμβάνουσιν.
sentences.literal_english: Good judges do not take gifts.
sentences.smooth_english: Good judges do not take gifts.

sentences.greek: μὴ ἴδοιμεν τὴν πόλιν διεφθαρμένην.
sentences.literal_english: May we not see our city destroyed!
sentences.smooth_english: May we not see our city destroyed!

sentences.greek: οὐκ ὄψει τοὺς βασιλέα ἀποκτείναντας.
sentences.literal_english: You will not see those who killed the king.
sentences.smooth_english: You will not see those who killed the king.

sentences.greek: μὴ πορευθῇς εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς στρατιᾶς.
sentences.literal_english: Do not march into Greece with the same army.
sentences.smooth_english: Do not march into Greece with the same army.

sentences.greek: οὐκ εἴδομεν τοὺς τὰ τείχη διαφθείραντας.
sentences.literal_english: We did not see those who had destroyed the walls.
sentences.smooth_english: We did not see those who had destroyed the walls.

sentences.greek: τὰς αὐτὰς γυναῖκας ἐν τῷ νεῲ ὀψόμεθα.
sentences.literal_english: We shall see the same women in the temple.
sentences.smooth_english: We shall see the same women in the temple.

sentences.greek: οἱ ἀνδρειότατοι ναῦται οὐ πολλάκις ποιηταὶ γίγνονται.
sentences.literal_english: The bravest sailors do not often become poets.
sentences.smooth_english: The bravest sailors do not often become poets.

sentences.greek: τὴν πόλιν λαβὼν μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς στρατιᾶς ἀφίκετο.
sentences.literal_english: Having taken the city, he arrived with the same army.
sentences.smooth_english: Having taken the city, he arrived with the same army.

sentences.greek: ὁ Σωκράτης αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐβούλετο ἰδεῖν αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: Socrates himself did not wish to see him.
sentences.smooth_english: Socrates himself did not wish to see him.

sentences.greek: τὰ αὐτὰ ἐροῦμεν τοῖς στρατιώταις καὶ ναύταις.
sentences.literal_english: We shall say the same things to the soldiers and the sailors.
sentences.smooth_english: We shall say the same things to the soldiers and the sailors.

sentences.greek: οἱ τὸν βασιλέα ἰδόντες ἐθαύμασαν τὴν ἀρετὴν αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: Those who saw the king admired his courage.
sentences.smooth_english: Those who saw the king admired his courage.

sentences.greek: λάβωμεν τὴν πόλιν καὶ τροπαῖον στήσωμεν.
sentences.literal_english: Let us take the city and set up a trophy.
sentences.smooth_english: Let us take the city and set up a trophy.

sentences.greek: οἱ σοφώτατοι οὐκ ἀεὶ τὰ αὐτὰ λέγουσιν.
sentences.literal_english: The wisest men do not always say the same things.
sentences.smooth_english: The wisest men do not always say the same things.

sentences.greek: τὴν πόλιν λαβόντες τοῖς Ἀθηναίοις ἔδωκαν.
sentences.literal_english: Having taken the city, they gave it to the Athenians.
sentences.smooth_english: Having taken the city, they gave it to the Athenians.

sentences.greek: εἰς τὴν νῆσον ἀφικόμενοι ἀνδρειότατα ἐμαχέσαντο.
sentences.literal_english: Having arrived in the island they fought most bravely.
sentences.smooth_english: Having arrived in the island they fought most bravely.

sentences.greek: οἱ δῶρα λαμβάνοντες οὐκ ἀεὶ τιμῶσι τοὺς δόντας.
sentences.literal_english: Those who take gifts do not always honour those who give them.
sentences.smooth_english: Those who take gifts do not always honour those who give them.

sentences.greek: ὁ ποιητὴς σοφώτερον εἶπε τοῦ ῥήτορος.
sentences.literal_english: The poet spoke more wisely than the orator.
sentences.smooth_english: The poet spoke more wisely than the orator.

sentences.greek: ἐβουλόμεθα πλεῖστα αἰτεῖν.
sentences.literal_english: We wished to ask for very many things.
sentences.smooth_english: We wished to ask for very many things.

sentences.greek: οἱ ὅπλα λαβόντες ὑπὸ τῶν φυλάκων ἀπέθανον.
sentences.literal_english: Those who took arms were killed by the guards.
sentences.smooth_english: Those who took arms were killed by the guards.

sentences.greek: τοὺς νεὼς ἰδόντες οὐ μενοῦμεν ἐν τῇ πόλει.
sentences.literal_english: Having seen the temples we shall not remain in the city.
sentences.smooth_english: Having seen the temples we shall not remain in the city.

sentences.greek: οἱ τὴν θεὰν ἰδόντες ἀποθανοῦνται.
sentences.literal_english: Those who see the goddess will die.
sentences.smooth_english: Those who see the goddess will die.

sentences.greek: ὁ αὐτὸς στρατηγὸς εἶδεν ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ νήσῳ.
sentences.literal_english: The same general saw us in the island.
sentences.smooth_english: The same general saw us in the island.

sentences.greek: ἐκεῖναι αἱ πόλεις ὑπὸ τοῦ αὐτοῦ στρατιώτου διεφθάρησαν.
sentences.literal_english: Those cities were destroyed by the same soldier.
sentences.smooth_english: Those cities were destroyed by the same soldier.

sentences.greek: ἀποκτενοῦμεν τοὺς τὴν πόλιν προδόντας.
sentences.literal_english: We shall kill those who betrayed the city.
sentences.smooth_english: We shall kill those who betrayed the city.

sentences.greek: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησε τὸν κόσμον, δηλαδή, τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, πάντα τὰ ζῶα, καὶ πάντας τοὺς καρπούς.
sentences.literal_english: In beginning the God made the world, that is, the heaven and the earth, all the living-things, and all the fruits.
sentences.smooth_english: In the beginning God made the world, that is, the heaven and the earth, all the animals, and all the fruits.

sentences.greek: Ἔπειτα ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησε τὸν ἄνθρωπον κατὰ εἰκόνα Θεοῦ, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτόν, Ἀδάμ.
sentences.literal_english: Then the God made the man according to image of God, and called him, Adam.
sentences.smooth_english: Then God made man in the image of God, and called him Adam.

sentences.greek: Ἐκ πλευρᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ ἐποίησε καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα· ἐκάλεσεν αὐτήν, Εὔαν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ Ἀδάμ.
sentences.literal_english: Out of a rib from the Adam he made also the woman; he called her, Eve, and gave her to the Adam.
sentences.smooth_english: Out of a rib from Adam He also made the woman; He called her Eve, and gave her to Adam.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ἐτεθείκει τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα ἐν κήπῳ ἡδίστῳ, ὃς ὀνομάζεται Παράδεισος.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand God had placed the man and the woman in a garden most sweet, which is named Paradise.
sentences.smooth_english: And God had placed the man and the woman in a most pleasant garden, which is called Paradise.

sentences.greek: Ὅ γε ἄνθρωπός ἐστιν ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ Θεοῦ, διότι δύναται γινώσκειν καὶ φιλεῖν Θεόν.
sentences.literal_english: The indeed man is the image of the God, because he is able to know and to love God.
sentences.smooth_english: Man indeed is the image of God, because he is able to know and to love God.

sentences.greek: Πρότερον μέν, ἔνιοι ἦσαν τῶν ἀγγέλων οἵ, τετυφωμένοι τῷ φρονήματι, ἀπέστησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ· ὁ δὲ κατέβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὰ ἔνερθεν.
sentences.literal_english: Formerly on the one hand, some were of the angels who, having been puffed up in the mind, stood away from the God; the on the other hand [he] cast down them into the beneath.
sentences.smooth_english: Previously, there were some of the angels who, being puffed up with pride, departed from God; and He cast them down to the lower regions.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν φρονιμώτατος τούτων τῶν ἀφισταμένων, λαβὼν τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ ὄφεως, εἶπε τῇ γυναικί· Τί οὖν οὐ γεύεσθε τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ξύλου, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Παραδείσου;
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand most prudent of these standing away, having taken the form of the serpent, said to the woman: Why then do you not taste of the fruit of the tree, which is in middle of the Paradise?
sentences.smooth_english: The wisest of these who departed, having taken the form of a serpent, said to the woman: Why then do you not eat of the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the Paradise?

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ γυνή· Ὅτι ὁ Θεός, ἔφη, ἀπαγορεύει ἡμῖν τοῦτο ποιεῖν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand woman: Because the God, she said, forbids to us this to do.
sentences.smooth_english: And the woman said: Because God, she said, forbids us to do this.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ ὄφις εἶπεν· Ἐὰν φάγητε τοῦτον τὸν καρπόν, οὐκ ἀποθανεῖσθε.
sentences.literal_english: And the serpent said: If you should eat this the fruit, not will you die.
sentences.smooth_english: And the serpent said: If you eat this fruit, you will not die.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ γυνὴ τότε ἔφαγε τὸν καρπόν, καὶ ἔδωκεν ἀπὸ τούτου τῷ ἀνδρί.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand woman then ate the fruit, and gave from this to the husband.
sentences.smooth_english: Then the woman ate the fruit, and gave some of it to her husband.

sentences.greek: Τοιγαροῦν ὁ Κύριος καταρᾶται μὲν τῷ ὄφει, ἐκβάλλει δὲ τὸν Ἀδὰμ καὶ τὴν Εὔαν τοῦ Παραδείσου.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the Lord curses on the one hand the serpent, casts out on the other hand the Adam and the Eve from the Paradise.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore, the Lord cursed the serpent, and cast Adam and Eve out of Paradise.

sentences.greek: Ἔπειτα ἡ Εὔα ἔτεκε δύο παῖδας, τὸν Καϊν καὶ τὸν Ἄβελ.
sentences.literal_english: Then the Eve bore two children, the Cain and the Abel.
sentences.smooth_english: Then Eve bore two children, Cain and Abel.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἄβελ ἦν ποιμὴν προβάτων, ὁ δὲ Κάϊν ἐγεώργει.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Abel was a shepherd of sheep, the on the other hand Cain farmed.
sentences.smooth_english: Abel was a shepherd of sheep, but Cain tilled the ground.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὁ Κάϊν, φθονῶν τῷ ἀδελφῷ, ἐφόνευσε τὸν Ἄβελ.
sentences.literal_english: But the Cain, envying the brother, murdered the Abel.
sentences.smooth_english: But Cain, envying his brother, killed Abel.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Θεὸς εἶπε τῷ Κάϊν· Ποῦ ἔστιν ὁ ἀδελφός σου;
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand God said to the Cain: Where is the brother of you?
sentences.smooth_english: God said to Cain: Where is your brother?

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Κάϊν· Οὐκ οἶδα, ἔφη· εἰμὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ φύλαξ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ;
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Cain: Not do I know, he said; am for I a guard of the brother?
sentences.smooth_english: And Cain replied: I do not know; am I my brother’s keeper?

sentences.greek: Ἐνταῦθα ὁ Κύριος εἶπε· Φωνὴ αἵματος τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου βοᾷ πρός με ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐγὼ καταράομαί σοι.
sentences.literal_english: Thereupon the Lord said: A voice of blood of the brother of you cries out toward me out of the earth, and I curse to you.
sentences.smooth_english: Then the Lord said: The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground, and I curse you.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ Εὔα ἔτεκεν ἄλλον υἱόν, ὃν ἐπωνόμασε Σήθ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Eve bore another son, whom she named Seth.
sentences.smooth_english: Eve bore another son, whom she named Seth.

sentences.greek: Οἱ μὲν ἀπόγονοι τοῦ Κάϊν, οἱ καλούμενοι Παῖδες ἀνθρώπων, πονηροὶ ἦσαν· οἱ δὲ ἀπόγονοι τοῦ Σὴθ ἐκαλοῦντο Παῖδες Θεοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand descendants of the Cain, the ones being called Children of men, wicked were; the on the other hand descendants of the Seth were being called Children of God.
sentences.smooth_english: The descendants of Cain, called the Children of Men, were wicked; but the descendants of Seth were called the Children of God.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Θεός, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἡ τῶν ἀνθρώπων πονηρία καθ᾽ ἡμέραν αὔξεται, ἐβουλεύσατο διαφθείρειν πάντα ὅσα ἐπεποιήκει.
sentences.literal_english: And the God, having seen that the of the men wickedness according to day increases, purposed to destroy all things as many as he had made.
sentences.smooth_english: And God, seeing that the wickedness of men increased day by day, resolved to destroy all that he had made.

sentences.greek: Ἐφείσατο μέντοι τοῦ Νῶε, ὃς ἦν ἀγαθὸς τὸν θυμόν.
sentences.literal_english: He spared however of the Noah, who was good the spirit.
sentences.smooth_english: However, he spared Noah, who was good in spirit.

sentences.greek: Καὶ γὰρ ὁ Νῶε, Θεοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἐποίησεν ἐκ ξύλων κιβωτὸν μεγίστην, ἣν ἤλειψεν ἐντὸς καὶ ἔξω ἀσφάλτῳ.
sentences.literal_english: And for the Noah, of God having commanded, made out of woods an ark greatest, which he smeared inside and outside with pitch.
sentences.smooth_english: For Noah, at God’s command, made a very great ark out of wood, which he coated inside and out with pitch.

sentences.greek: Αὐτίκα ὁ Νῶε εἰςῆλθεν εἰς τὴν κιβωτὸν αὐτός, καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἡ γυνή, καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ Σήμ, Χάμ, Ἰαφέθ, καὶ αἱ νυοί.
sentences.literal_english: Immediately the Noah entered into the ark himself, and with him the woman, and the sons Shem, Ham, Japheth, and the daughters-in-law.
sentences.smooth_english: Immediately Noah entered the ark, he himself, and with him his wife, and his sons Shem, Ham, Japheth, and their wives.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Νῶε εἰσήγαγεν ἔτι εἰς αὐτὴν ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν θηρίων δύο, τὸν ἄῤῥενα καὶ τὴν θήλειαν.
sentences.literal_english: And the Noah led in still into it from all of the wild-beasts two, the male and the female.
sentences.smooth_english: And Noah also brought into it two of every kind of animal, the male and the female.

sentences.greek: Εὐθὺς μὲν πάντα τὰ ὕδατα τῆς γῆς ἐκφέρεται, καὶ ἅμα ὁ ὑετὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γίνεται τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ τοσαύτας νύκτας.
sentences.literal_english: Straightaway on the one hand all the waters of the earth are carried out, and at the same time the rain from the heaven becomes forty days and as many nights.
sentences.smooth_english: At once all the waters of the earth burst forth, and at the same time rain fell from heaven for forty days and as many nights.

sentences.greek: Πάντα δὲ τότε ὅσα ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καταλύεται.
sentences.literal_english: All things on the other hand then as many as were upon the earth are destroyed.
sentences.smooth_english: Then all things that were on the earth were destroyed.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ κιβωτὸς ἐπεφέρετο ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand ark was being carried upon the water.
sentences.smooth_english: But the ark floated upon the water.

sentences.greek: Ἐπεὶ τέλος ὁ Νῶε ἔγνω ὅτι τὸ ὕδωρ ἀνεχώρησεν, ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς κιβωτοῦ· καί, βωμὸν ἱδρύσας, τῷ Θεῷ παρέσχε χαριστήρια.
sentences.literal_english: When finally the Noah knew that the water withdrew, he went out out of the ark; and, an altar having founded, to the God he provided thank-offerings.
sentences.smooth_english: When at last Noah knew that the water had receded, he went out from the ark; and, having built an altar, he offered thanksgiving to God.

sentences.greek: Ἥ γε πίστις πρὸς Θεὸν καὶ ὁ νόμος, ὁ ἀληθινός, διέμειναν παρά τισι τῶν ἁγιωτάτων ἀνδρῶν.
sentences.literal_english: The indeed faith toward God and the law, the true, remained beside some of the most holy men.
sentences.smooth_english: Faith in God and the true law remained among some of the holiest men.

sentences.greek: Ἐν οἷς καὶ ἦν Ἀβραάμ, ὃς μὲν κατῴκει ἐν πόλει τῶν Χαλδαίων· ἐκεῖ δὲ ὁ Κύριος συμμαχίαν ἐποιήσατο πρὸς αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: In whom also was Abraham, who on the one hand was dwelling in a city of the Chaldeans; there on the other hand the Lord made an alliance toward him.
sentences.smooth_english: Among them was Abraham, who lived in the city of the Chaldeans; and there the Lord made a covenant with him.

sentences.greek: Ὕστερον μὲν ὁ Θεὸς αὐτὸν ἐκέλευσε μετοικεῖν, λέγων· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ Θεός σου· ἴσθι ἐνώπιον ἐμοῦ, καὶ γίνου ἄμεμπτος.
sentences.literal_english: Later on the one hand the God commanded him to migrate, saying: I am the God of you; be before me, and become blameless.
sentences.smooth_english: Later, God ordered him to migrate, saying: I am your God; be before me, and be blameless.

sentences.greek: Ἀνάβλεψον δὴ εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, καὶ ἀρίθμησον τοὺς ἀστέρας, εἰ δυνήσῃ· οὕτως ἔσται τὸ γένος σου. Καὶ ἐγὼ εὐλογήσω, σοῦ ἕνεκα, πάντα τὰ τῆς γῆς ἔθνη.
sentences.literal_english: Look up indeed into the heaven, and number the stars, if you will be able; thus will be the offspring of you. And I will bless, on account of you, all the nations of the earth.
sentences.smooth_english: Look up to the sky, and count the stars, if you can; so shall your descendants be. And I will bless, for your sake, all the nations of the earth.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἀβραὰμ εἰς Συχέμ ἀφικόμενος, ἐκεῖ Θεῷ ἵδρυσε βωμόν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Abraham into Shechem having arrived, there to God founded an altar.
sentences.smooth_english: And Abraham, having arrived at Shechem, there built an altar to God.

sentences.greek: Ἀβραὰμ μέν ποτε, περὶ μεσημβρίαν, καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῆς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς, εἶδεν ἄφνω τρεῖς ἄνδρας ἐναντίον ἑστηκότας.
sentences.literal_english: Abraham on the one hand once, around midday, sitting upon the door of the tent, saw suddenly three men opposite having stood.
sentences.smooth_english: Once, Abraham, sitting at the door of his tent at noon, suddenly saw three men standing opposite him.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἔλεγεν ἑνὶ τῶν τριῶν· Κύριε, εἰ ἄρα εὗρον χάριν παρὰ σοῦ, μὴ παρέλθῃς τὴν θύραν. Ἐγώ γε ὕδωρ κομίσω, καὶ νίψω τοὺς πόδας ὑμῶν, καὶ σῖτον καὶ ποτὸν ὑμῖν προςοίσω.
sentences.literal_english: And he was saying to one of the three: Lord, if then I found favor beside you, not pass by the door. I at least water will bring, and will wash the feet of you, and food and drink to you will bring toward.
sentences.smooth_english: And he said to one of the three: Lord, if I have found favor with you, do not pass by the door. I will bring water and wash your feet, and I will bring you bread and drink.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δέ, ἐπειδὴ ἔφαγον, εἶπον πρὸς τὸν Ἀβραάμ· Σάῤῥα, ἡ γυνή σου, ἕξει υἱόν.
sentences.literal_english: The ones on the other hand, after they ate, said toward the Abraham: Sarah, the wife of you, will have a son.
sentences.smooth_english: And after they had eaten, they said to Abraham: Sarah, your wife, will have a son.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν ἡ Σάῤῥα ἤκουσε τοῦτο καὶ ἐγέλασεν· ἦν γὰρ ἤδη πρεσβυτέρα.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the Sarah heard this and laughed; she was for already older.
sentences.smooth_english: So Sarah heard this and laughed; for she was already old.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπεπιστεύκει τῷ Θεῷ τοιαῦτα ἐπαγγελλομένῳ.
sentences.literal_english: But Abraham had trusted in the God such things promising.
sentences.smooth_english: But Abraham had faith in God who promised such things.

sentences.greek: Διόπερ ἡ Σάῤῥα ἔτεκεν υἱὸν ἐν τῷ γήρᾳ, καὶ ἦν ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἰσαάκ.
sentences.literal_english: Because of which the Sarah bore a son in the old age, and was a name to him Isaac.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore Sarah bore a son in her old age, and his name was Isaac.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Θεὸς βουλόμενος πειρᾶν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀβραάμ, Ἀβραάμ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand God wishing to test the Abraham, said to him: Abraham, Abraham.
sentences.smooth_english: God, wishing to test Abraham, said to him: Abraham, Abraham.

sentences.greek: Ἀβραὰμ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ.
sentences.literal_english: Abraham on the other hand answered: Behold I.
sentences.smooth_english: And Abraham answered: Here I am.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος· Λάβε, ἔφη, τὸν υἱόν σου, τὸν μονογενῆ, τὸν ἀγαπητόν, καὶ πορευθείς, θῦσον αὐτὸν ὁλόκαυστον, ἐφ᾿ ἓν τῶν ὀρέων ὧν σοι δείξω.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Lord: Take, he said, the son of you, the only-begotten, the beloved, and having gone, sacrifice him a whole-burnt-offering, upon one of the mountains of which to you I will show.
sentences.smooth_english: And the Lord said: Take, he said, your son, your only-begotten, your beloved, and go, offer him as a burnt offering, on one of the mountains which I will show you.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε Ἀβραὰμ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη, αὐτός τε καὶ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ, πρὸς τὸ ὄρος, τὸ δεικνύμενον.
sentences.literal_english: And then Abraham having stood up went, himself both and the son of him, toward the mountain, the being shown.
sentences.smooth_english: And then Abraham arose and went, he and his son, to the mountain that was shown.

sentences.greek: Ἐπὶ δὲ ἄκρου ὄρεος, ὁ πατήρ, ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα, ἐλάμβανεν ἤδη τὴν μάχαιραν.
sentences.literal_english: Upon on the other hand top of a mountain, the father, having stretched out the hand, was taking already the knife.
sentences.smooth_english: And on the top of the mountain, the father, stretching out his hand, was already taking the knife.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ἄγγελός τις ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τὴν αὐτοῦ χεῖρα ἐπέσχε.
sentences.literal_english: But a messenger certain out of heaven the of him hand held back.
sentences.smooth_english: But an angel from heaven restrained his hand.

sentences.greek: Θεῷ γὰρ ἀπέχρησεν ἡ θυσία κριοῦ τινος, ἀντὶ τῆς τοῦ Ἰσαάκ.
sentences.literal_english: To God for was sufficient the sacrifice of a ram certain, instead of the of the Isaac.
sentences.smooth_english: For the sacrifice of a certain ram sufficed for God, instead of that of Isaac.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἀβραὰμ γηραιότατος ἐγένετο· ὁ δὲ Κύριος ηὐλόγησεν αὐτὸν κατὰ πάντα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Abraham oldest became; the on the other hand Lord blessed him according to all things.
sentences.smooth_english: Abraham had become very old; and the Lord had blessed him in all things.

sentences.greek: Ἀβραὰμ δὲ τοῦτο προςέταξε τῷ Ἐλιέζερ, τῷ ἄρχοντι πάντων τῶν αὐτοῦ· Πορεύθητι εἰς τὴν γῆν, οὗ ἐγεννήθην, καὶ λαβὼν ἐκεῖθεν γυναῖκα, ἄγε τῷ υἱῷ μου Ἰσαάκ.
sentences.literal_english: Abraham on the other hand this commanded to the Eliezer, to the ruler of all the things of him: Go into the land, where I was born, and having taken from there a woman, lead to the son of me Isaac.
sentences.smooth_english: Abraham gave this command to Eliezer, the chief of all his household: Go to the land where I was born, and taking a wife from there, bring her for my son Isaac.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἐλιέζερ δέκα καμήλους συναπήγαγε, καὶ ταχέως εἰς τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν ἀπεδήμησεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Eliezer ten camels led away together, and swiftly into the Mesopotamia went abroad.
sentences.smooth_english: Eliezer took ten camels and quickly departed for Mesopotamia.

sentences.greek: Ἀφικόμενος δὲ ἐκεῖσε, παρέστη αὐτὸς παρὰ φρέατι ὕδατος· καί, Θεοῦ σημαίνοντος, ᾔσθετο παρθένον, τὸ ὄνομα Ῥεβέκκα, τὴν Βαθουήλ, μέλλουσαν εἶναι γυναῖκα τῷ Ἰσαάκ.
sentences.literal_english: Having arrived on the other hand there, stood he beside a well of water; and, of God showing a sign, he perceived a virgin, the name Rebecca, the of Bethuel, being about to be wife to the Isaac.
sentences.smooth_english: When he arrived there, he stood by a well of water; and, with God giving a sign, he recognized a maiden, named Rebecca, daughter of Bethuel, who was to become Isaac’s wife.

sentences.greek: Τοιγαροῦν Ἐλιέζερ τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτὴν ᾔτησεν· οἱ δὲ τῷ Ἐλιέζερ τὸ αἴτημα ἐχαρίσαντο.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore Eliezer the parents her asked; the ones on the other hand to the Eliezer the request granted.
sentences.smooth_english: So Eliezer asked her parents; and they granted Eliezer his request.

sentences.greek: Ἰσαὰκ δὴ ἔγημεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἐφίλησεν.
sentences.literal_english: Isaac indeed married her, and loved.
sentences.smooth_english: Isaac then married her, and loved her.

sentences.greek: Τῷ μὲν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τῇ Ῥεβέκκᾳ ἐγένετο δίδυμα παιδία, Ἡσαῦ καὶ Ἰακώβ, ὃς καὶ ἐπωνομάσθη Ἰσραήλ.
sentences.literal_english: To the on the one hand Isaac and to the Rebecca became twin children, Esau and Jacob, who also was named Israel.
sentences.smooth_english: Isaac and Rebecca had twin children, Esau and Jacob, who was also called Israel.

sentences.greek: Τὼ γοῦν παῖδε ηὐξηθήτην. Ὁ μὲν Ἡσαῦ ἐπιστήμων ἦν τοῦ κυνηγεῖν, καὶ ἀγροῖκος· ὁ δὲ Ἰακὼβ ἦν ἁπλοῦς, καὶ οἴκοι διέτριβε.
sentences.literal_english: The at any rate two children grew. The on the one hand Esau skilled was of the to hunt, and rustic; the on the other hand Jacob was simple, and at home spent time.
sentences.smooth_english: The two boys grew up. Esau was skilled in hunting and was rustic; but Jacob was simple and stayed at home.

sentences.greek: Μάλιστα μὲν Ἰσαὰκ ἐφίλησεν Ἡσαῦ, ὅτι τροφὴν ἔσχεν ἐκ θήρας αὐτοῦ· τὸν δὲ Ἰακὼβ ἡ Ῥεβέκκα ἐφίλησεν.
sentences.literal_english: Most on the one hand Isaac loved Esau, because food he had out of hunting of him; the on the other hand Jacob the Rebecca loved.
sentences.smooth_english: Isaac especially loved Esau, because he had food from his hunting; but Rebecca loved Jacob.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ τοῦ Ἡσαῦ τὰ πρωτοτόκια τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἀποδομένου, ὁ μὲν Ἰσαὰκ ηὐλόγησεν Ἰακώβ, εἰπών· Γίνου κύριος τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
sentences.literal_english: But of the Esau the birthrights to the brother giving away, the on the one hand Isaac blessed Jacob, having said: Become lord of the brother of you.
sentences.smooth_english: But when Esau gave his birthright to his brother, Isaac blessed Jacob, saying: Be lord over your brother.

sentences.greek: Ἡσαῦ δὲ ὠργίσθη τῷ Ἰακὼβ διὰ ταύτην τὴν εὐλογίαν.
sentences.literal_english: Esau on the other hand was angered to the Jacob on account of this the blessing.
sentences.smooth_english: Esau was angry with Jacob because of this blessing.

sentences.greek: Διότι Ῥεβέκκα, περὶ τῷ Ἰακὼβ σφόδρα δεδοικυῖα, διέγνω πέμπειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν.
sentences.literal_english: Because Rebecca, about the Jacob exceedingly having feared, decided to send him into the Mesopotamia.
sentences.smooth_english: Because Rebecca, being greatly afraid for Jacob, decided to send him to Mesopotamia.

sentences.greek: Τούτῳ δὲ ὁδοιποροῦντι, ὁ Κύριος πανταχοῖ παρακολουθήσειν ὑπέσχετο.
sentences.literal_english: To this one on the other hand journeying, the Lord everywhere to follow promised.
sentences.smooth_english: And as he journeyed, the Lord promised to be with him everywhere.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Ἰακὼβ ἦλθεν εἰς Χαῤῥάν, ὅπου εἶδε παρὰ φρέατι ποιμένας ἀναπαυομένους. Οἱ δὲ ποιμένες ἔδειξαν αὐτῷ Ῥαχήλ, τὴν τοῦ Λάβαν.
sentences.literal_english: And the Jacob went into Haran, where he saw beside a well shepherds resting. The on the other hand shepherds showed to him Rachel, the of the Laban.
sentences.smooth_english: Jacob came to Haran, where he saw shepherds resting by a well. The shepherds showed him Rachel, Laban’s daughter.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Λάβαν ἐξέδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ Ἰακώβ, ὃς ἀδελφιδοῦς ἦν αὐτῷ.
sentences.literal_english: And the Laban gave out her to the Jacob, who a nephew was to him.
sentences.smooth_english: Laban gave her to Jacob, who was his nephew.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ἐγέννησε δώδεκα υἱούς, ἐν οἷς ἦσαν Ῥουβήν, Συμεών, Λευί, Ἰούδας, Ἰωσὴφ, καὶ ὕστερον, Βενιαμίν, καὶ θυγατέρα μίαν, Δείναν.
sentences.literal_english: The Jacob begot twelve sons, in whom were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Joseph, and later, Benjamin, and daughter one, Dinah.
sentences.smooth_english: Jacob fathered twelve sons, among whom were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Joseph, and later Benjamin, and one daughter, Dinah.

sentences.greek: Καὶ μετὰ τὴν τοῦ Ἰακὼβ ἐπάνοδον εἰς Χεβρών, εἰς τὴν Χαναὰν χώραν, ἡ Ῥαχὴλ ἐτελεύτησεν ἐν τῷ τίκτειν τὸν Βενιαμίν.
sentences.literal_english: And after the of the Jacob return into Hebron, into the Canaan country, the Rachel ended in the to bear the Benjamin.
sentences.smooth_english: And after Jacob’s return to Hebron, in the land of Canaan, Rachel died while giving birth to Benjamin.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἰακὼβ ἐν τῇ γῇ Χαναὰν κατῴκει σὺν τοῖς υἱοῖς· τὸν δὲ Ἰωσὴφ ἠγάπα ὑπὲρ πάντας.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Jacob in the land Canaan was dwelling with the sons; the on the other hand Joseph he loved over all.
sentences.smooth_english: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan with his sons; he loved Joseph more than all the others.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, ζηλοτυποῦντες, αὐτὸν σφόδρα ἐμίσησαν, καὶ μάλιστα, δυοῖν ἕνεκα ὀνείροιν, οἷς προὐσημαίνετο αὐτὸν πάντων τῶν ἄλλων κρατήσειν.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the brothers of him, being jealous, him exceedingly hated, and especially, of two on account of dreams, by which it was foretold him of all of the others to rule.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore, his brothers, being jealous, hated him greatly, especially because of two dreams, which foretold that he would rule over all the others.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἰακὼβ αὐτὸν ἀπέστειλε πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς Συχέμ· οἱ δὲ τὰ πρόβατα τοῦ πατρὸς ἔνεμον.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Jacob him sent toward the brothers of him into Shechem; the ones on the other hand the sheep of the father were pasturing.
sentences.smooth_english: Jacob sent him to his brothers in Shechem; they were tending their father’s sheep.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε οὗτοι προεῖδον τὸν Ἰωσὴφ μακρόθεν, καὶ ἐβουλεύσαντο ἀποκτεῖναι αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: And then these foresaw the Joseph from afar, and planned to kill him.
sentences.smooth_english: Then they saw Joseph from afar and plotted to kill him.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ῥουβὴν συνεβούλευσεν ἐμβάλλειν αὐτὸν εἰς ἕνα τῶν λάκκων, τῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἐλπίζων ἐξαιρήσειν αὐτὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἐπανάξειν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Reuben advised to cast in him into one of the pits, the ones in the desert, hoping to take out him and toward the father to lead back.
sentences.smooth_english: Reuben advised them to throw him into one of the pits in the wilderness, hoping to rescue him and return him to their father.

sentences.greek: Ἐνταῦθα δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἐπώλησαν ὁδοιπόροις ἐς Αἴγυπτον ἐρχομένοις.
sentences.literal_english: Here on the other hand the brothers the Joseph sold to wayfarers into Egypt going.
sentences.smooth_english: There, the brothers sold Joseph to travelers going to Egypt.

sentences.greek: Διόπερ ὁ Ἰακὼβ πεπεισμένος τὸν Ἰωσήφ, τὸν φίλτατον, τεθνηκότα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὀδύνης ἐστρέφθη.
sentences.literal_english: Because of which the Jacob having been persuaded the Joseph, the dearest, having died, over the pain was turned.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore Jacob, convinced that Joseph, his dearest, was dead, was overcome with grief.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε Πετεφρής τις, ἀνὴρ Αἰγύπτιος, ὠνήσατο τὸν Ἰωσήφ, ὡς δοῦλον· καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἔστι μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ, κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ πάντα τὸν οἶκον.
sentences.literal_english: And then Potiphar a certain, a man Egyptian, bought the Joseph, as a slave; and having seen that the God is with him, set down him upon all the house.
sentences.smooth_english: And then a certain Potiphar, an Egyptian man, bought Joseph as a slave; and seeing that God was with him, he appointed him over his whole household.

sentences.greek: Τῆς δὲ γυναικὸς τοῦ Πετεφροῦ αἰτίαν ψευδῆ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ ἐπαγαγούσης, ἐκεῖνος εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν ἐνεβλήθη, ὅπου συνέκρινε τὰ ἐνύπνια τοῦ τε ἀρχισιτοποιοῦ καὶ τὰ τοῦ ἀρχιοινοχόου τοῦ Φαραὼ βασιλέως.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the other hand wife of the Potiphar a charge false to the Joseph having brought on, that one into the prison was cast in, where he interpreted the dreams of the both chief-baker and the ones of the chief-cupbearer of the Pharaoh king.
sentences.smooth_english: But when Potiphar’s wife brought a false accusation against Joseph, he was thrown into prison, where he interpreted the dreams of both Pharaoh’s chief baker and chief cupbearer.

sentences.greek: Μετὰ δὲ δύο ἔτη, καὶ Φαραὼ ἐνύπνιον εἶδεν. Ὅ γε ἀρχιοινοχόος τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ ἐμνήσθη.
sentences.literal_english: After on the other hand two years, also Pharaoh a dream saw. The at least chief-cupbearer of the Joseph remembered.
sentences.smooth_english: After two years, Pharaoh also had a dream. Then the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε ἐκεῖνος προὐσήμανεν ἑπτὰ ἔτη λιμοῦ γενήσεσθαι μετὰ ἑπτὰ ἔτη ἀφθονίας.
sentences.literal_english: And then that one foretold seven years of famine to be about to become after seven years of abundance.
sentences.smooth_english: And then he foretold that seven years of famine would come after seven years of abundance.

sentences.greek: Θαυμάσας οὖν ὁ Φαραὼ τοιαύτην τοῦ ἀνδρὸς σοφίαν, τῷ Ἰωσὴφ εἶπεν· Σὺ ἔσῃ ἐπὶ τῷ οἴκῳ μου, καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὑπακούσεταί σοι. Ἰδοὺ καθίστημί σε σήμερον ἐπὶ πάσῃ γῇ Αἰγύπτου.
sentences.literal_english: Having marveled therefore the Pharaoh such of the man wisdom, to the Joseph he said: You will be upon the house of me, and all the people will obey to you. Behold I set down you today upon all land of Egypt.
sentences.smooth_english: Pharaoh, amazed at such wisdom in the man, said to Joseph: You shall be over my house, and all my people shall obey you. Behold, I appoint you this day over all the land of Egypt.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν ὁ Ἰωσὴφ συνήγαγε σῖτον πολὺν σφόδρα.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the Joseph gathered together grain much exceedingly.
sentences.smooth_english: So Joseph gathered very much grain.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὰ ἑπτὰ ἔτη ἀφθονίας, δεινότατος ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.
sentences.literal_english: But after the seven years of abundance, most terrible became a famine in all the earth.
sentences.smooth_english: But after the seven years of abundance, a most severe famine arose in all the land.

sentences.greek: Κατέβησαν δὲ δέκα ἀδελφοὶ τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ εἰς τὴν Αἴγυπτον, τοῦ πατρὸς κελεύσαντος.
sentences.literal_english: Went down on the other hand ten brothers of the Joseph into the Egypt, of the father having commanded.
sentences.smooth_english: Then ten brothers of Joseph went down to Egypt, at their father’s command.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἰωσὴφ ἐπέγνω τοὺς ἀδελφούς, αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Joseph recognized the brothers, they on the other hand not recognized him.
sentences.smooth_english: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ κακῶς αὐτοῖς ἐχρήσατο πρῶτον, εἰπών· Κατάσκοποί ἐστε.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand badly to them used first, having said: Spies you are.
sentences.smooth_english: At first he treated them harshly, saying: You are spies.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Δώδεκα ἐσμὲν ἀδελφοί· ὁ μὲν νεώτατος, ὁ Βενιαμίν, τῷ πατρὶ παραμένει· ὁ δὲ ἕτερος οὐκ ἔτι ζῇ.
sentences.literal_english: The ones on the other hand said: Twelve we are brothers; the on the one hand youngest, the Benjamin, to the father remains beside; the on the other hand other not still lives.
sentences.smooth_english: But they said: We are twelve brothers; the youngest, Benjamin, remains with our father; the other is no longer alive.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἀμφὶ τοῦ φιλτάτου Βενιαμίν δεδοικώς, τὸν μὲν Συμεῶνα κατέσχε, προςειπών· Ἴτε, καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν ὑμῶν, τὸν νεώτατον, πρός με ἀγάγετε.
sentences.literal_english: But the Joseph about the dearest Benjamin having feared, the on the one hand Simeon held down, having addressed: Go, and the brother of you, the youngest, toward me lead.
sentences.smooth_english: But Joseph, being concerned about his dearest Benjamin, detained Simeon, saying to them: Go, and bring your brother, the youngest one, to me.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ τῷ Ἰακὼβ ταῦτα προςήνεγκαν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand brothers to the Jacob these things brought toward.
sentences.smooth_english: And the brothers reported these things to Jacob.

sentences.greek: Ἀκούσας ταῦτα, ὁ Ἰακὼβ τότε ἀνεβόα· Ὦ Βενιαμίν, παιδίον θυμῷ γλυκύτατον, οὐ καταβήσῃ εἰς τὴν Αἴγυπτον.
sentences.literal_english: Having heard these things, the Jacob then was crying out: O Benjamin, child to spirit most sweet, not will you go down into the Egypt.
sentences.smooth_english: When Jacob heard this, he cried out: O Benjamin, child sweetest to my heart, you shall not go down to Egypt.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ δὲ λιμοῦ καθ᾿ ἡμέραν αὐξανομένου, καὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ πείσαντος, ὁ Ἰακὼβ τέλος εἴασε καὶ τὸν Βενιαμὶν σὺν ἀδελφοῖς ἀπέρχεσθαι.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the other hand famine according to day increasing, and of the Judah the father of him having persuaded, the Jacob finally allowed also the Benjamin with brothers to go away.
sentences.smooth_english: But as the famine increased day by day, and Judah persuaded his father, Jacob finally allowed Benjamin to go with his brothers.

sentences.greek: Ἐταράχθη δὲ Ἰωσὴφ εἰς τὴν ὄψιν τοῦ Βενιαμίν.
sentences.literal_english: Was troubled on the other hand Joseph into the sight of the Benjamin.
sentences.smooth_english: Joseph was moved at the sight of Benjamin.

sentences.greek: Πᾶσι μὲν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς φιλοφρονεῖται· βουλόμενος δὲ μέντοι τὸν Βενιαμίν κατέχειν, κλοπὴν αὐτῷ ἐγκαλεῖ, καὶ δουλοῖ αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: To all on the one hand the brothers he shows affection; wishing on the other hand however the Benjamin to hold down, theft to him he calls in, and enslaves him.
sentences.smooth_english: He treated all his brothers kindly; but wishing, however, to detain Benjamin, he accused him of theft and enslaved him.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἰούδας· Νῦν οὖν, ἔφη, ἐὰν ἀνελεύσωμαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἄνευ τοῦ Βενιαμίν, ὑπὸ τῆς λύπης ἀποθανεῖται. Ἔγωγε δουλεύσω σοι ἀντὶ τοῦ παιδίου.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Judah: Now therefore, he said, if I should go back toward the father without the Benjamin, by the grief he will die. I at least will be a slave to you instead of the child.
sentences.smooth_english: Then Judah said: Now then, if I return to my father without Benjamin, he will die from grief. I myself will serve you instead of the boy.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἰωσήφ, οὐκέτι ἑαυτοῦ κρατῶν, εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰωσήφ· ἔτι ὁ πατήρ μου ζῇ;
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Joseph, no longer of himself having power, said: I am Joseph; still the father of me lives?
sentences.smooth_english: But Joseph, no longer able to restrain himself, said: I am Joseph; is my father still alive?

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐπιπεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Βενιαμίν, καὶ καταφιλήσας πάντας τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ, ἐδάκρυεν.
sentences.literal_english: And having fallen upon upon the neck of the Benjamin, and having kissed all the brothers of him, he was weeping.
sentences.smooth_english: And falling upon Benjamin’s neck, and kissing all his brothers, he wept.

sentences.greek: Ἔλεγε δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἀναλαβόντες τὸν πατέρα, ἥκετε πρός με· τὰ γὰρ πάντα τῆς Αἰγύπτου χρήματα ὑμῖν ἔσται.
sentences.literal_english: He was saying on the other hand toward them: Having taken back the father, have come toward me; the for all of the Egypt things to you will be.
sentences.smooth_english: He said to them: Bring your father and come to me; for all the wealth of Egypt shall be yours.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν ὁ Ἰακὼβ περιχαρὴς ἐγένετο· καὶ ἀναλαβὼν πάντα, ἃ ἐκτήσατο ἐν γῇ Χαναάν, εἰςῆλθεν εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἐκεῖ τέλος τὸν φίλτατον υἱὸν πάλιν εὗρεν.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the Jacob very joyful became; and having taken back all things, which he acquired in land Canaan, he entered into Egypt; and there finally the dearest son again he found.
sentences.smooth_english: So Jacob became exceedingly joyful; and taking all that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, he entered Egypt; and there at last he found his dearest son again.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Φαραὼ τὴν γῆν Γεσὲμ αὐτῷ ἐδωρήσατο καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Pharaoh the land Goshen to him gifted and to the sons of him.
sentences.smooth_english: And Pharaoh gave him and his sons the land of Goshen.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ Ἰσραήλ, ὥσπερ κλάδοι, ἐπληθύνθησαν, καὶ πλεῖστον κατίσχυον, καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐπλήρουν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand sons of Israel, just as branches, were multiplied, and most prevailed, and the land filled.
sentences.smooth_english: The sons of Israel, like branches, multiplied, and became very strong, and filled the land.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ τότε ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος, ὃς οὐκ ἐγίνωσκε τὸν Ἰωσήφ.
sentences.literal_english: But then stood up king another, who not knew the Joseph.
sentences.smooth_english: But then a different king arose, who did not know Joseph.

sentences.greek: Εἶπε δὲ τῷ ἔθνει αὐτοῦ· Οἱ τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ υἱοἱ μέγα πλῆθός εἰσι, καὶ μεῖζον ἡμῶν ἰσχύουσι. Πιέσωμεν οὖν αὐτούς, μὴ πλείους γίνωνται.
sentences.literal_english: He said on the other hand to the nation of him: The of the Israel sons a great multitude are, and greater of us they are strong. Let us press therefore them, lest more they become.
sentences.smooth_english: He said to his people: The sons of Israel are a great multitude, and they are stronger than us. Let us oppress them, so that they do not become more numerous.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐκέλευσε τὰς μαιευτρίας ἀναιρεῖν νεογνούς, τοὺς ἄῤῥενας τῶν Ἑβραίων.
sentences.literal_english: And he commanded the midwives to destroy newborns, the males of the Hebrews.
sentences.smooth_english: And he ordered the midwives to kill the newborns, the male children of the Hebrews.

sentences.greek: Τότε γυνή τις ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Λευὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν, καλὸν τὸ πρόςωπον, ὃν μὲν τρεῖς μῆνας ἔκρυψε· μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα, ἐν κοιτίδι ἐξέθηκε τὸ τέκνον παρὰ τὸν Νεῖλον.
sentences.literal_english: Then woman a certain out of the tribe Levi bore a son, beautiful the face, whom on the one hand three months she hid; after on the other hand these things, in a basket she put out the child beside the Nile.
sentences.smooth_english: Then a woman from the tribe of Levi bore a son, beautiful in appearance, whom she hid for three months; afterwards, she placed the child in a basket by the Nile.

sentences.greek: Ἰδοῦσα δὲ τὸ τέκνον ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραώ, Μωϋσῆν ἐπωνόμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ υἱὸν ἐποιήσατο.
sentences.literal_english: Having seen on the other hand the child the daughter of Pharaoh, Moses named him, and son made.
sentences.smooth_english: When Pharaoh’s daughter saw the child, she named him Moses, and made him her son.

sentences.greek: Ἐπειδὴ ὁ Μωϋσῆς ἀνὴρ ἐγένετο, ἐξῆλθε πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ, τοὺς Ἑβραίους.
sentences.literal_english: Since the Moses a man became, he went out toward the brothers of him, the Hebrews.
sentences.smooth_english: When Moses became a man, he went out to his brothers, the Hebrews.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν λύπην αὐτῶν, ἐβουλεύσατο ἐξάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῆς Αἰγύπτου.
sentences.literal_english: And having seen the grief of them, he decided to lead out them out of the Egypt.
sentences.smooth_english: And seeing their suffering, he decided to lead them out of Egypt.

sentences.greek: Εἰςῆλθεν οὖν Μωϋσῆς πρὸς Φαραώ, τοῦ Θεοῦ κελεύσαντος· ἐκεῖνος δὲ πρῶτον ἠρνήσατο.
sentences.literal_english: Entered therefore Moses toward Pharaoh, of the God having commanded; that one on the other hand first denied.
sentences.smooth_english: So Moses went to Pharaoh, at God’s command; but at first, Pharaoh refused.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὡς εἶδε τὰ πολλὰ σημεῖα, ἃ Κύριος ἐποίησε, καὶ ἔτυχεν ὀρφανὸς ὢν ἑνὸς τῶν παίδων, τότε φοβηθείς, εἶπε τῷ Μωϋσῇ καὶ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ Ἀαρών· Ἀνάστητε καὶ ἐξέλθετε, καὶ ὑμεῖς, καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραήλ. Λατρεύσατε, κατὰ τὴν ὑμῶν γνώμην, Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ ὑμῶν.
sentences.literal_english: But as he saw the many signs, which Lord made, and happened an orphan being of one of the children, then having feared, he said to the Moses and to the brother of him Aaron: Stand up and go out, also you, and the sons of Israel. Serve, according to the of you judgment, to Lord to the God of you.
sentences.smooth_english: But when he saw the many signs that the Lord performed, and suffered the loss of one of his children, then, afraid, he said to Moses and his brother Aaron: Rise up and go out, you and the sons of Israel. Worship, as you wish, the Lord your God.

sentences.greek: Οἱ μὲν Ἑβραῖοι ἀπεδήμησαν, καὶ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὸ μέσον τοῦ ἐρυθραίου πελάγεος, κατὰ τὸ ξηρόν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Hebrews went abroad, and entered into the middle of the Red Sea, according to the dry.
sentences.smooth_english: The Hebrews departed, and entered into the midst of the Red Sea, on dry ground.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ Αἰγύπτιοι, διώκοντες αὐτούς, κατὰ τῆς θαλάσσης πάντες κατεδύοντο.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Egyptians, pursuing them, down from the sea all were submerged.
sentences.smooth_english: But the Egyptians, pursuing them, all perished in the sea.

sentences.greek: Ἦν δέ, πέραν θαλάσσης, ὄρος τι, τοὔνομα Σινά.
sentences.literal_english: Was on the other hand, beyond sea, mountain a certain, the name Sinai.
sentences.smooth_english: Now, beyond the sea, there was a certain mountain, named Sinai.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐπειδὴ οἱ Ἑβραῖοι ἐκεῖσε ἀφίκοντο, ἐποιήσαντο μὲν στρατόπεδον.
sentences.literal_english: And since the Hebrews there arrived, they made on the one hand a camp.
sentences.smooth_english: And when the Hebrews arrived there, they set up camp.

sentences.greek: Μωϋσῆς δὲ ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος, ὅπου ὁ Θεὸς ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ τὰ δέκα ἅγια ῥήματα, τὸν Δεκάλογον.
sentences.literal_english: Moses on the other hand went up into the mountain, where the God gave to him the ten holy words, the Decalogue.
sentences.smooth_english: But Moses went up the mountain, where God gave him the ten holy words, the Decalogue.

sentences.greek: Ταῦτα μὲν τὰ ῥήματα, ἃ τὰ πρῶτα γράφεται, εἰς τὸν Θεὸν προςήκει, τὰ δὲ ἄλλα εἰς τὸν πλησίον. Ὁ δὲ νόμος εἰς δύο λιθίνας πλάκας ἐγράφη.
sentences.literal_english: These on the one hand the words, which the first are written, into the God pertain, the on the other hand others into the neighbor. The on the other hand law into two stone tablets was written.
sentences.smooth_english: These words, the first of which pertain to God, and the others to one’s neighbor. The law was written on two stone tablets.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ἰδὼν ὁ λαὸς ὅτι βραδύνει ὁ Μωϋσῆς καταβῆναι ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους, συνέστη, καὶ τῷ Ἀαρών· Ἀνάστηθι, ἔφη, καὶ ποίησον ἡμῖν θεούς, οἳ προβήσονται ἡμῶν.
sentences.literal_english: But having seen the people that delays the Moses to go down out of the mountain, stood together, and to the Aaron: Stand up, he said, and make to us gods, who will step forward of us.
sentences.smooth_english: But when the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain, they gathered together and said to Aaron: “Arise,” they said, “and make us gods who will go before us.”

sentences.greek: Ὃ δὲ ἐποίησεν αὐτοῖς μόσχον χρυσοῦν, ὃν οἱ Ἑβραῖοι προςεκύνησαν.
sentences.literal_english: Who on the other hand made to them a calf golden, which the Hebrews worshipped.
sentences.smooth_english: So he made for them a golden calf, which the Hebrews worshipped.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Κύριος ὀργισθεὶς ἀναιρεῖ τότε εἰς τριςχιλίους ἄνδρας.
sentences.literal_english: And the Lord having been angered destroys then into three thousand men.
sentences.smooth_english: And the Lord, being angered, then destroyed about three thousand men.

sentences.greek: Προςέτι ὁ Κύριος τῷ Μωϋσεῖ· Τὸν δεκάλογον κατακλείσεις ἐν κιβωτῷ τινι· καὶ ἐν σκηνῇ τινι τὴν κιβωτὸν θήσεις.
sentences.literal_english: Besides the Lord to the Moses: The Decalogue you will shut down in an ark certain; and in a tent certain the ark you will place.
sentences.smooth_english: Furthermore, the Lord said to Moses: “You shall place the Decalogue in a certain ark, and in a certain tent you shall put the ark.”

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Μωϋσῆς κιβωτὸν ἐποιήσατο ξύλων ἀσήπτων, καταχρυσωθεῖσαν ἔσωθεν καὶ ἔξωθεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Moses an ark made of woods rot-proof, having been gilded within and without.
sentences.smooth_english: So Moses made an ark of incorruptible wood, overlaid with gold inside and out.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε ᾠκοδόμησε σκηνήν, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἔθηκε λυχνίαν χρυσῆν, καὶ τράπεζαν χρυσίου, καὶ θυσιαστήριον τῶν θυμιαμάτων.
sentences.literal_english: And then he built a tent, in which also he placed a lampstand golden, and a table of gold, and an altar of the incenses.
sentences.smooth_english: And then he built a tent, in which he placed a golden lampstand, a golden table, and an altar of incense.

sentences.greek: Καὶ προςεῖπεν ὁ Θεός· Ἵδρυε ἔξωθεν θυσιαστήριον τῶν καρπωμάτων χαλκοῦν παρὰ ταῖς θύραις τῆς σκηνῆς. Συλλάμβανε τόν τε Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποίει αὐτοῖς στολὰς ἁγίας.
sentences.literal_english: And addressed the God: Found outside an altar of the whole-burnt-offerings bronze beside the doors of the tent. Take together the both Aaron and the sons of him, and make to them robes holy.
sentences.smooth_english: And God said: “Set up outside an altar of burnt offerings of bronze by the doors of the tent. Take Aaron and his sons, and make holy garments for them.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τοιαῦτα ἔσεται τάδε τὰ ἱμάτια· ποιήσεις τὸ περιστήθιον, καὶ τὸν ποδήρη, καὶ χιτῶνα λινοῦν, καὶ τὴν ἐπωμίδα, καὶ κίδαριν, καὶ ζώνην.
sentences.literal_english: And such will be these the garments; you will make the breastpiece, and the long robe, and a tunic linen, and the ephod, and a turban, and a belt.
sentences.smooth_english: And these shall be the garments: you shall make the breastplate, the robe, the linen tunic, the ephod, the turban, and the sash.

groups.group_title: 21. The Festivals of the Hebrews. – Nadab and Abihu.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εἶπεν ἔτι πρὸς Μωϋσῆν· Καὶ λέγε πρὸς τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ· Τοιαῦται ἔσονται αἱ ἑορταί, ἃς ἁγίας καλέσετε.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Lord said still toward Moses: And say toward the sons of Israel: Such will be the festivals, which holy you will call.
sentences.smooth_english: And the Lord spoke again to Moses: And say to the sons of Israel: These shall be the festivals, which you shall call holy.

sentences.greek: Ἓξ μὲν ἡμέρας πονήσετε· τῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ, Σάββατον, παύσεσθε πάντων τῶν πόνων.
sentences.literal_english: Six on the one hand days you will toil; on the on the other hand day the seventh, Sabbath, you will cease of all the toils.
sentences.smooth_english: For six days you shall labor; but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, you shall rest from all work.

sentences.greek: Ἐν τῇ τεσσαρεςκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ πρώτου μηνός, τελέσετε τὸ Πάσχα, τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου δίοδον.
sentences.literal_english: In the fourteenth day of the first month, you will fulfill the Passover, the of the Lord passing through.
sentences.smooth_english: On the fourteenth day of the first month, you shall celebrate the Passover, the passage of the Lord.

sentences.greek: Ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ Πάσχα πεντήκοντα ἡμέρας ἀριθμήσετε, καὶ νέαν ἑορτὴν ποιήσετε, μνήμῃ φυλάξοντες τὸν νόμον, τὸν ἐν Σινὰ συγχωρούμενον.
sentences.literal_english: From on the other hand the Passover fifty days you will number, and a new festival you will make, in memory to guard the law, the in Sinai being conceded.
sentences.smooth_english: From the Passover, you shall count fifty days, and you shall hold a new festival, keeping in memory the law given on Sinai.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἀαρὼν καὶ δύο υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ, Ναδὰβ καὶ Ἀβιούδ, τῷ Θεῷ τὰ ἱερὰ ἔῤῥεξαν. Ἀλλὰ τούτων ἑκάτερος, τὸ πυρεῖον λαβόντες, προςήνεγκαν Κυρίῳ πῦρ βέβηλον.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Aaron and two sons of him, Nadab and Abihu, to the God the sacred things did. But of these each, the fire-pan having taken, brought toward to Lord fire profane.
sentences.smooth_english: And Aaron and his two sons, Nadab and Abihu, performed the sacred rites to God. But each of them, taking the censer, offered profane fire to the Lord.

sentences.greek: Ἀπέθανον οὖν αὐτίκα, παράδειγμα φοβερὸν τοῖς Ἑβραίοις.
sentences.literal_english: They died therefore immediately, an example fearful to the Hebrews.
sentences.smooth_english: They died immediately, a fearful example to the Hebrews.

sentences.greek: Ὡς δὲ οἱ Ἑβραῖοι, κάμνοντες τῇ ὁδοιπορίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἠθύμησαν, εἰς τοῦτο ἦλθον ὕβρεως, ὥστε λέγειν πρὸς Μωϋσῆν· Βουλεύεις ἀποκτεῖναι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄρτος ἡμῖν, οὔτε ὕδωρ.
sentences.literal_english: As on the other hand the Hebrews, toiling in the journeying in the desert, were discouraged, into this they came of insolence, so as to say toward Moses: You plan to kill us in the desert, since not is bread to us, neither water.
sentences.smooth_english: As the Hebrews, weary from their journey in the desert, became disheartened, they went so far as to say to Moses: You intend to kill us in the desert, since we have neither bread nor water.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Κύριος, καίπερ ἀγανακτῶν ὑπὲρ τούτων, ἐπέβαλεν ἐπὶ τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὄρτυγας ἀφθόνως. Οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ τὸν λαὸν ἐπάταξε πληγὴν μεγάλην σφόδρα.
sentences.literal_english: The Lord, although being indignant over these things, cast upon upon the camp quails abundantly. Not indeed but the people he struck a plague great exceedingly.
sentences.smooth_english: The Lord, though angered by them, sent an abundance of quails upon the camp. Nevertheless, He struck the people with a very great plague.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἔπειτα προςεῖπεν· Οὗτοι, πλῆθος πονηρόν, ἐπανέστησαν ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ· ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ταύτῃ ἐκεῖ ἀποθανοῦνται.
sentences.literal_english: And then addressed: These, a multitude wicked, stood up against upon me; in the desert this there they will die.
sentences.smooth_english: And then He said: These, a wicked multitude, have risen up against Me; in this desert, there they shall die.

sentences.greek: Αὐτὸς μὲν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Ναβαῦ, ὅθεν εἶδε πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν τὴν ἐπηγγελμένην· καὶ ἐτελεύτησε, τοῦ Κυρίου κελεύσαντος.
sentences.literal_english: Himself on the one hand the Moses went up upon the mountain Nebo, whence he saw all the land the having been promised; and ended, of the Lord having commanded.
sentences.smooth_english: Moses himself ascended Mount Nebo, from where he saw all the promised land; and he died, as the Lord had commanded.

sentences.greek: Ἔκλαυσαν δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ τριάκοντα ἡμέρας.
sentences.literal_english: Wept for on the other hand him the sons of Israel thirty days.
sentences.smooth_english: The sons of Israel mourned him for thirty days.

groups.group_title: 23. Jesus – The crossing of the Jordan.

sentences.greek: Μετὰ τὴν τελευτὴν τοῦ Μωϋσέως, ὁ Κύριος τὸν Ἰησοῦν προςαγορεύων, ἔφη· Νῦν οὖν ἀναστάς, διάβηθι τὸν Ἰορδάνην. Πᾶς ὁ τόπος, ὃν ὑμεῖς ἂν καταπατήσητε, ὑμέτερος ἔστω.
sentences.literal_english: After the end of the Moses, the Lord the Joshua addressing, said: Now therefore having stood up, cross the Jordan. All the place, which you if you should tread down, yours let be.
sentences.smooth_english: After the death of Moses, the Lord addressing Jesus said: Now then, arise, cross the Jordan. Every place that you tread upon shall be yours.

sentences.greek: Σὺ δέ, Ἰησοῦ, ἴσχυε καὶ ἀνδρίζου· κληρωσάμενος, διαμερίσεις τῷ λαῷ ταύτην τὴν γῆν.
sentences.literal_english: You on the other hand, Joshua, be strong and act like a man; having received by lot, you will divide to the people this the land.
sentences.smooth_english: But you, Jesus, be strong and courageous; having cast lots, you will divide this land among the people.

sentences.greek: Διῆλθον δὲ κήρυκες διὰ τῆς παρεμβολῆς, λέγοντες· Ὅταν ἴδητε τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ τοὺς ἱερεῖς, τοὺς Λευίτας, αἴροντας αὐτήν, ὀπίσω πορεύσεσθε, καὶ οὕτω διαβήσεσθε τὸν Ἰορδάνην, κατὰ τὸ ξηρόν.
sentences.literal_english: Went through on the other hand heralds through the camp, saying: Whenever you should see the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the priests, the Levites, lifting it, backward you will go, and thus you will cross the Jordan, according to the dry.
sentences.smooth_english: Then heralds went through the camp, saying: When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the priests, the Levites, carrying it, you shall follow after it, and thus you will cross the Jordan on dry ground.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.
sentences.literal_english: And these things became.
sentences.smooth_english: And so it happened.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ οὐκ ἦν πόλις, ἣν οὐκ ἔλαβεν Ἰσραήλ, οὐδὲ βασιλεύς, ὃν οὐκ ὤλεσεν, ὃν τρόπον εἶπεν ὁ Κύριος.
sentences.literal_english: But not was a city, which not took Israel, neither a king, whom not he destroyed, which manner said the Lord.
sentences.smooth_english: But there was no city that Israel did not take, nor king whom they did not destroy, just as the Lord had said.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἔτι ζῶντος, οἱ μὲν υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ πάντες τῷ Θεῷ ἐλάτρευσαν πιστῶς· οἱ γὰρ πρεσβύτεροι αὐτῶν ἔγνωσαν πάντα τὰ ἔργα Κυρίου, ὅσα ἐποίησεν οὗτος τοῦ λαοῦ χάριν.
sentences.literal_english: Of the Joshua still living, the on the one hand sons of Israel all to the God served faithfully; the for elders of them knew all the works of Lord, as many as made this one of the people on account.
sentences.smooth_english: While Jesus was still alive, all the sons of Israel faithfully served God; for their elders had known all the works of the Lord, which He had done for the sake of the people.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐτελεύτησε καὶ αὐτός, ἑκατὸν δέκα ἔτη γεγονώς.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Joshua ended also himself, a hundred ten years having become.
sentences.smooth_english: But Jesus also died, being one hundred and ten years old.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε οἱ Ἑβραῖοι τὸν Κύριον, τὸν Θεὸν τῶν πατέρων αὐτῶν, ἐγκατέλιπον, τὸν ἐξαγαγόντα αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῆς γῆς Αἰγύπτου, καὶ προςέτι τοὺς τῶν ἐθνῶν θεοὺς προςεκύνησαν.
sentences.literal_english: And then the Hebrews the Lord, the God of the fathers of them, left behind, the having led out them out of the land of Egypt, and besides the of the nations gods worshipped.
sentences.smooth_english: Then the Hebrews abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and moreover worshipped the gods of the nations.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ὀργισθεὶς παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς εἰς χεῖρας τῶν ἐχθρῶν, καὶ ἐξέθλιψεν αὐτοὺς σφόδρα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand God having been angered gave over them into hands of the enemies, and squeezed out them exceedingly.
sentences.smooth_english: And God, being angered, delivered them into the hands of their enemies, and oppressed them greatly.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὁ Κύριος ἐνίοτε ἤγειρεν αὐτοῖς κριτάς, ἵνα σώσαιεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ χειρὸς τῶν ἐχθρῶν, τῶν ἐκθλιβόντων αὐτούς.
sentences.literal_english: But the Lord sometimes raised up to them judges, in order that they might save them out of hand of the enemies, the ones squeezing out them.
sentences.smooth_english: But the Lord sometimes raised up judges for them, in order to save them from the hand of their enemies, those who oppressed them.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ μὲν κριτοῦ ζῶντος, ἤκουεν ὁ Κύριος τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ στεναγμῶν· ὡς δὲ ἀπέθνησκε κριτής, πάλιν οἱ Ἑβραῖοι τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ περιέπιπτον, πρὸς τὸ ἔσχατον τῆς κακίας ὑποφερόμενοι, καὶ ἔτι ὑπὲρ τοὺς πατέρας αὐτῶν.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the one hand judge living, heard the Lord the of the people groans; as on the other hand died a judge, again the Hebrews into the sin fell around, toward the extremity of the wickedness being carried under, and still over the fathers of them.
sentences.smooth_english: While the judge was alive, the Lord listened to the groans of the people; but when the judge died, again the Hebrews fell into sin, being brought to the utmost wickedness, even more than their fathers.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε ὁ Κύριος ἐπὶ τοῖς γεγενημένοις ὀργιζόμενος, εἶπε τοῖς Ἑβραίοις· Ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε τῆς φωνῆς μου, ἐγὼ οὐκ ἀναιρήσω ἄνδρα ἕνα ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν ὧν κατέλιπεν Ἰησοῦς, ὁπότε ἀπέθανεν.
sentences.literal_english: And then the Lord upon the things having become being angered, said to the Hebrews: Since not you heard the voice of me, I not will take up a man one out of the nations which left behind Joshua, when he died.
sentences.smooth_english: And then the Lord, being angry at what had happened, said to the Hebrews: Since you have not listened to my voice, I will not remove a single man from the nations which Joshua left behind when he died.

sentences.greek: Οὗτοι δὲ ἐν τοῖς κριταῖς λόγου ἄξιοι, Γεδεών, Ἰεφθαέ, Σάμψων, Ἡλί τε καὶ Σαμουήλ.
sentences.literal_english: These on the other hand in the judges of word worthy, Gideon, Jephthah, Samson, Eli both and Samuel.
sentences.smooth_english: These, among the judges who are worthy of mention, are Gideon, Jephthah, Samson, Eli, and Samuel.

sentences.greek: Καὶ πάλιν παρενόμησαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ διέφθειρον οἱ Μαδιηναῖοι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῶν.
sentences.literal_english: And again transgressed the sons of Israel, and destroyed the Midianites the fruits of them.
sentences.smooth_english: And again the sons of Israel acted lawlessly, and the Midianites destroyed their crops.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ἐβόησαν οἱ Ἰσραηλῖται πρὸς τὸν Κύριον, ὃς ἐξαπέστειλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Γεδεών.
sentences.literal_english: But cried out the Israelites toward the Lord, who sent forth to them the Gideon.
sentences.smooth_english: But the Israelites cried out to the Lord, who sent them Gideon.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Γεδεὼν κατέσχε μόνον παρ᾿ ἑαυτῷ στρατιὰν μικράν, νυκτὸς δὲ ἦλθε πρὸς τὴν τῶν Μαδιηναίων παρεμβολήν.
sentences.literal_english: The Gideon held down only beside to himself an army small, of night on the other hand he came toward the of the Midianites camp.
sentences.smooth_english: Gideon kept only a small army with him, and at night he came to the camp of the Midianites.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐκεῖ ἤκουσε στρατιώτου ἑτέρῳ διηγουμένου ὄνειρον, ἐξ οὗ εἴκασε τὴν ἑαυτοῦ νίκην.
sentences.literal_english: And there he heard of a soldier to another detailing a dream, out of which he guessed the of himself victory.
sentences.smooth_english: There he heard a soldier telling another a dream, from which he inferred his own victory.

sentences.greek: Πρίν γε τὴν μάχην συνάπτειν, τοῖς τριακοσίοις ἀνδράσιν αἱρετοῖς λαμπάδας ἔδωκεν ἡμμένας, καὶ σάλπιγγας.
sentences.literal_english: Before at least the battle to join, to the three hundred men chosen torches he gave having been lit, and trumpets.
sentences.smooth_english: Before joining battle, he gave the chosen three hundred men burning torches and trumpets.

sentences.greek: Ὡς δὲ ἐγγὺς ἐγένοντο, συντρίψαντες τὰς λαμπάδας, ἀνεβόησαν λέγοντες· Ξίφος τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ τοῦ Γεδεών!
sentences.literal_english: As on the other hand near they became, having shattered the torches, they cried out saying: A sword of the Lord and of the Gideon!
sentences.smooth_english: When they came near, breaking the torches, they shouted, saying: The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!

sentences.greek: Οἱ γοῦν πολέμιοι φοβηθέντες ἔφυγον, καὶ ἀλληλοκτονήσαντες διεφθάρησαν.
sentences.literal_english: The therefore enemies having feared fled, and having killed one another were destroyed.
sentences.smooth_english: So the enemies, terrified, fled, and having killed each other, were destroyed.

sentences.greek: Κατ᾿ ἐκείνους τοὺς χρόνους, ὅτε οἱ κριταὶ ἦρχον, ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἐν τῇ γῇ· καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἀνήρ τις σὺν δυοῖν υἱοῖν εἰς ἀγρὸν Μωάβ· ὄνομα δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ Ἐλιμέλεχ.
sentences.literal_english: According to those the times, when the judges were ruling, became a famine in the land; and went a man certain with two sons into field of Moab; name on the other hand to the man Elimelech.
sentences.smooth_english: In those days, when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land; and a certain man went with his two sons to the land of Moab; the man’s name was Elimelech.

sentences.greek: Τοῦδε τοῦ ἀνδρὸς ἀποθανόντος, οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ, οἳ ἐγεγαμήκεισαν Ὀρφὰ καὶ Ῥούθ, γυναῖκας Μωαβίτιδας, καὶ αὐτοὶ δέκα ἔτη ὕστερον ἀπέθανον.
sentences.literal_english: Of this the man having died, the sons of him, who had married Orpah and Ruth, women Moabite, also themselves ten years later died.
sentences.smooth_english: After this man died, his sons, who had married Orpah and Ruth, Moabite women, also died ten years later.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ Νωεμίν, ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ Ἐλιμέλεχ, ἀκούσασα ὅτι ἐπέσκεπται ὁ Κύριος τὸν λαόν, ἀνέστη αὐτή, σὺν ταῖν νυοῖν αὐτῆς, ἐπιστρέψαι εἰς τὴν γῆν Ἰούδα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Naomi, the wife of the Elimelech, having heard that has visited the Lord the people, stood up herself, with the two daughters-in-law of her, to turn upon into the land of Judah.
sentences.smooth_english: Naomi, the wife of Elimelech, having heard that the Lord had visited His people, arose with her daughters-in-law to return to the land of Judah.

sentences.greek: Ὡς δὲ ὁδὸν ἐχώρησαν, τότε ἡ Νωεμὶν αὐταῖς· Ἐπιστράφητε, ἔφη, πρὸς τὴν μητέρα ὑμῶν.
sentences.literal_english: As on the other hand a way they proceeded, then the Naomi to them: Turn upon, she said, toward the mother of you.
sentences.smooth_english: As they were on their way, Naomi said to them: Return, she said, to your mother.

sentences.greek: Κατεφίλησεν Ὀρφὰ μὲν τὴν πενθερὰν αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀπῆλθεν· ἡ δὲ Ῥοὺθ ἠκολούθησε τῇ Νωεμίν.
sentences.literal_english: Kissed down Orpah on the one hand the mother-in-law of her, and went away; the on the other hand Ruth followed to the Naomi.
sentences.smooth_english: Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and departed; but Ruth followed Naomi.

sentences.greek: Ἦν δὲ ἐν τῇ γῇ Ἰσραὴλ ἀνήρ τις, τοὔνομα Βοόζ, συγγενὴς ὢν τῷ ἀνδρὶ Νωεμίν, τῷ Ἐλιμέλεχ.
sentences.literal_english: Was on the other hand in the land of Israel a man certain, the name Boaz, a relative being to the husband of Naomi, to the Elimelech.
sentences.smooth_english: Now there was in the land of Israel a man named Boaz, a relative of Naomi’s husband, Elimelech.

sentences.greek: Καὶ εἶπεν ἡ Ῥοὺθ τῇ Νωεμίν· Ἡμεῖς μὲν πάντων ἀποροῦμεν· πορεύσομαι δὴ ἐγώ, εἴ σοι τοῦτο φίλον, καὶ σταχυολογήσω.
sentences.literal_english: And said the Ruth to the Naomi: We on the one hand of all things are at a loss; will go indeed I, if to you this pleasing, and will glean ears of corn.
sentences.smooth_english: And Ruth said to Naomi: We are in need of everything; I will go, if it pleases you, and glean.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ Νωεμὶν ἀπεκρίνατο· Πορεύου, θύγατερ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Naomi answered: Go, daughter.
sentences.smooth_english: Naomi replied: Go, my daughter.

sentences.greek: Ὡς οὖν ἐσταχυολόγει αὕτη, ὁ μὲν Βοόζ, ᾧ ὁ ἀγρὸς ὑπῆρχε, κατὰ τύχην ἐλθὼν ἐκ Βηθλεέμ, τοῖς θερίζουσιν ἔλεξε· Κύριος μεθ᾿ ὑμῶν!
sentences.literal_english: As therefore was gleaning ears of corn this one, the on the one hand Boaz, to whom the field belonged, according to chance having come out of Bethlehem, to the ones reaping said: Lord with of you!
sentences.smooth_english: As she was gleaning, Boaz, to whom the field belonged, happened to come from Bethlehem and said to the reapers: The Lord be with you!

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ εἶπον αὐτῷ· Εὐλογείτω σε Κύριος!
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand ones said to him: Let bless you Lord!
sentences.smooth_english: And they said to him: The Lord bless you!

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Βοὸζ προςεῖπε· Τίς αὕτη ἡ κόρη;
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Boaz addressed: Who this the maiden?
sentences.smooth_english: Boaz said: Who is this young woman?

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ ἀπεκρίναντο· Ἡ παῖς ἡ Μωαβῖτίς ἐστιν, ἡ ἀποστραφεῖσα μετὰ Νωεμὶν ἐκ τῆς γῆς Μωάβ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand ones answered: The child the Moabite is, the having turned back with Naomi out of the land of Moab.
sentences.smooth_english: They replied: She is the Moabite girl who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab.

sentences.greek: Καὶ Βοόζ, τῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ νόμῳ ὑπακούων, ἔλαβεν αὐτὴν εἰς γυναῖκα.
sentences.literal_english: And Boaz, to the of the God law obeying, took her into wife.
sentences.smooth_english: And Boaz, obeying the law of God, took her as his wife.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ ὕστερον ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ὃν ἐκάλεσαν Ὀβήδ, τὸν τοῦ Δαυὶδ προπάτορα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand later bore a son, whom they called Obed, the of the David forefather.
sentences.smooth_english: Later, she bore a son, whom they called Obed, the ancestor of David.

sentences.greek: Ὡς διετέλουν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀδικοῦντες, παρέδωκεν ὅδε αὐτοὺς ἐν χερσὶ τῶν Φιλισταίων.
sentences.literal_english: As continued the sons of Israel before of the Lord doing wrong, gave over this one them in hands of the Philistines.
sentences.smooth_english: As the sons of Israel continued to do wrong before the Lord, He delivered them into the hands of the Philistines.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὤφθη ἄγγελός τις ὑπὸ τῆς γυναῖκος τοῦ Μανωέ, ἀπὸ φυλῆς τοῦ Δάν, καὶ αὐτῇ· Σὺ στεῖρα, ἔφη· ἀλλὰ μετ᾿ ὀλίγον συλλήψῃ υἱόν.
sentences.literal_english: But was seen a messenger certain by the wife of the Manoah, from tribe of the Dan, and to her: You barren, he said; but after a little you will conceive a son.
sentences.smooth_english: But an angel appeared to the wife of Manoah, from the tribe of Dan, and said to her: "You are barren," he said, "but soon you will conceive a son."

sentences.greek: Καὶ προςεῖπεν· Ὅδε ὕστερον σώσει τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ἐκ χειρὸς τῶν Φιλισταίων.
sentences.literal_english: And addressed: This one later will save the Israel out of hand of the Philistines.
sentences.smooth_english: And he added: "He will later save Israel from the hand of the Philistines."

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ γυνή, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ ἀγγέλου πρόῤῥησιν, ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ὃν ἐκάλεσε Σάμψωνα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand woman, according to the of the messenger foretelling, bore a son, whom she called Samson.
sentences.smooth_english: The woman, according to the angel’s prophecy, bore a son, whom she called Samson.

sentences.greek: Ὡς οὖν τὸ παιδίον ηὐξήθη, ηὐλόγησεν αὐτὸ ὁ Κύριος· καί, νεανίας γεγονώς, τὸ σῶμα ἰσχυρότερος λέοντος ἐγένετο.
sentences.literal_english: As therefore the child grew, blessed him the Lord; and, a youth having become, the body stronger of a lion he became.
sentences.smooth_english: So as the child grew, the Lord blessed him; and, when he became a young man, his body became stronger than a lion.

sentences.greek: Ἔπειτα ὁ Σαμψὼν ἐκ τῶν Φιλισταίων γυναῖκα ἔλαβεν· ἐτήρει γὰρ εὐκαιρίαν, ὅπως βλάψαι ἂν αὐτούς.
sentences.literal_english: Then the Samson out of the Philistines a woman took; he was guarding for an opportunity, how to harm might them.
sentences.smooth_english: Then Samson took a wife from among the Philistines; for he was seeking an opportunity to harm them.

sentences.greek: Αὐτοὺς μὲν δεινὸν εἰργάσατο αὖθις καὶ αὖθις· καὶ ἐπάταξεν ἐξ αὐτῶν τριάκοντα ἄνδρας, καὶ ὕστερον χιλίους, καὶ τέλος ἐνέπρησε τὰ λήϊα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀμπέλους καὶ ἐλαίας.
sentences.literal_english: Them on the one hand a terrible thing he worked again and again; and he struck out of them thirty men, and later a thousand, and finally set on fire the crop fields of them, and vines and olive-trees.
sentences.smooth_english: He did terrible things to them again and again; he struck down thirty men among them, and later a thousand, and finally he burned their grain fields, vineyards, and olive groves.

sentences.greek: Ἔγημε μὲν Σάμψων γυναῖκα ἑτέραν, τοὔνομα Δαλιδά.
sentences.literal_english: Married on the one hand Samson woman another, the name Delilah.
sentences.smooth_english: Samson married another woman, named Delilah.

sentences.greek: Ἦλθον δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν οἱ ἄρχοντες, καὶ εἶπον· Ἀπάτησον τὸν ἄνδρα, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς δυνησώμεθα αὐτοῦ κρατεῖν.
sentences.literal_english: Came on the other hand toward her the rulers, and said: Deceive the husband, in order that also we may be able of him to have power.
sentences.smooth_english: The rulers came to her and said: "Deceive the man, so that we may be able to overpower him."

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ τῷ Σαμψῶνι· Λέγε δή μοι, ἔφη, ἐν τίνι ἡ ἰσχύς σου μεγάλη. Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐὰν δήσωσί με ἑπτὰ νευραῖς, ἀσθενὴς ἔσομαι ὡς εἷς τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand to the Samson: Say indeed to me, she said, in what the strength of you great. The on the other hand said: If they should bind me with seven bowstrings, weak I will be as one of the men.
sentences.smooth_english: And she said to Samson: "Tell me," she said, "what is the source of your great strength." He replied: "If they bind me with seven cords, I will be weak, like any other man."

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ἔψευδεν αὐτὴν τῷ λόγῳ.
sentences.literal_english: But he lied her in the word.
sentences.smooth_english: But he deceived her with his words.

sentences.greek: Τῇ δὲ λιπαρούσῃ ὅδε ὑπείκων τέλος, προςεῖπε· Διότι ὁ ξυρὸς οὐκ ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλήν μου.
sentences.literal_english: To the on the other hand entreating this one yielding finally, addressed: Because the razor not went up upon the head of me.
