sentences.smooth_english: Finally, yielding to her persistence, he said: "Because a razor has never come upon my head."

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν Δαλιδά, Σαμψῶνος βαθὺν καθεύδοντος, ἐκάλεσεν ἄνθρωπον, ὃς ἐξύρησε τὰς τρίχας τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἀπέστη ἡ ἰσχὺς ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore Delilah, of Samson deep sleeping, called a man, who shaved the hairs of the head of him. And stood away the strength from him.
sentences.smooth_english: So then Delilah, while Samson was sleeping deeply, called a man, who shaved the hair of his head. And his strength departed from him.

sentences.greek: Τὸν οὖν Σάμψωνα δεδεμένον οἱ Φιλισταῖοι εἰς φυλακὴν τίθενται.
sentences.literal_english: The therefore Samson having been bound the Philistines into prison place.
sentences.smooth_english: So the Philistines, having bound Samson, put him in prison.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὅ γε, πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν ἐκεῖ ἀνέλαβεν, ὅτι ἤρξατο ἡ κόμη αὐτοῦ βλαστάνειν.
sentences.literal_english: But he at least, all the power there took up again, because began the hair of him to sprout.
sentences.smooth_english: But there he regained all his strength, because his hair began to grow again.

sentences.greek: Τότε δὲ οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν Φιλισταίων συνήχθησαν θυσιάσαι καὶ εὐφρανθῆναι, λέγοντες· Ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεὸς ἐν χειρὶ ἡμῶν Σάμψωνα.
sentences.literal_english: Then on the other hand the rulers of the Philistines were gathered together to sacrifice and to be gladdened, saying: Gave the God in hand of us Samson.
sentences.smooth_english: Then the rulers of the Philistines gathered to sacrifice and to celebrate, saying: God has given Samson into our hands.

sentences.greek: Ὡς μὲν ἐκάλεσαν αὐτὸν ἐκ φυλακῆς, ἔστησαν ἀναμέσον τῶν κιόνων τοῦ οἴκου· ὁ δὲ Σαμψὼν ἔσεισε τοὺς δύο κίονας.
sentences.literal_english: As on the one hand they called him out of prison, they stood amidst of the columns of the house; the on the other hand Samson shook the two columns.
sentences.smooth_english: When they called him out of prison, they set him between the pillars of the house; and Samson shook the two pillars.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἔπεσε τότε ὁ οἶκος, καὶ ἦσαν οἱ τεθνηκότες τρισχίλιοι· ἔθανε δὲ καὶ αὐτός.
sentences.literal_english: And fell then the house, and were the ones having died three thousand; died on the other hand also himself.
sentences.smooth_english: And then the house fell, and those who died were three thousand; and he himself also died.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Σαμουὴλ ἐκ νηπίου καθιερώθη τῷ Θεῷ ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ· ἡ δὲ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτὸν μετὰ χεῖρας Ἡλὶ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, λέγουσα· Παρὰ Κυρίου ᾐτησάμην αὐτόν, καὶ ἔδωκέ μοι ὁ Κύριος τὸ αἴτημά μου.
sentences.literal_english: The Samuel out of infant was consecrated to the God by the mother of him; the on the other hand entrusted him with hands of Eli the high priest, saying: Beside of Lord I asked for myself him, and gave to me the Lord the request of me.
sentences.smooth_english: Samuel was dedicated to God from infancy by his mother; and she entrusted him to Eli the high priest, saying: I asked him from the Lord, and the Lord granted me my request.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, Ὀφνὶ καὶ Φινεές, ἠδίκησαν, οὐκ εἰδότες τὸν Κύριον.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand sons of the high priest, Hophni and Phinehas, did wrong, not knowing the Lord.
sentences.smooth_english: But the sons of the high priest, Hophni and Phinehas, acted unjustly, not knowing the Lord.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ Σαμουήλ ἦν λειτουργῶν ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ, χιτῶνα μικρὸν ἠμφιεσμένος, ὃν ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ, καὶ ἐμεγαλύνθη ἐνώπιον Κυρίου καὶ ἀνθρώπων.
sentences.literal_english: But Samuel was serving in the tent, a tunic small having been clothed, which made to him the mother, and was magnified before of Lord and of men.
sentences.smooth_english: But Samuel was serving in the tabernacle, clothed with a little tunic, which his mother made for him, and he grew in favor before the Lord and men.

sentences.greek: Διότι ὁ Θεὸς αὐτῷ ἀπεκάλυψε τὰ κακά, ὅσα ἂν πείσεται ὁ οἶκος τοῦ Ἡλί, διὰ τὰς τῶν υἱῶν ἁμαρτίας.
sentences.literal_english: Because the God to him uncovered the evils, as many as might suffer the house of the Eli, on account of the of the sons sins.
sentences.smooth_english: For God revealed to him the evils that would befall the house of Eli, because of the sins of his sons.

sentences.greek: Οἱ γὰρ τότε Ἰσραηλῖται ἐπιστρατείαν παρεσκευάσαντο ἐπὶ τοὺς Φιλισταίους.
sentences.literal_english: The for then Israelites an expedition prepared upon the Philistines.
sentences.smooth_english: For at that time the Israelites prepared for war against the Philistines.

sentences.greek: Ἔδοξε μὲν αὐτοῖς λαμβάνειν τὴν Θεοῦ κιβωτόν· ἐγένετο δὲ αὐτοῖς πληγὴ μεγάλη, καὶ ἔφυγον. Ἔπεσον γὰρ τριςμύριοι, καὶ Ὀφνὶ καὶ Φινεές· αὐτὴ δὲ ἡ κιβωτὸς ἑάλω.
sentences.literal_english: It seemed on the one hand to them to take the of God ark; became on the other hand to them a slaughter great, and they fled. Fell for thirty thousand, and Hophni and Phinehas; itself on the other hand the ark was taken.
sentences.smooth_english: It seemed good to them to take the Ark of God; but a great defeat happened to them, and they fled. For thirty thousand fell, and Hophni and Phinehas; and the Ark itself was captured.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ Σαμουὴλ ἤδη γεγηρακότος, συναθροίζονται ἄνδρες Ἰσραήλ, καὶ πορεύονται πρὸς αὐτόν, λέγοντες· Κατάστησον νῦν ἐφ᾿ ἡμᾶς βασιλέα, ὃς ἄρξει ἡμῶν.
sentences.literal_english: Of the Samuel already having grown old, gather together men of Israel, and go toward him, saying: Set down now upon us a king, who will rule of us.
sentences.smooth_english: When Samuel was already old, the men of Israel gathered together and went to him, saying: Appoint now over us a king, who will rule us.

sentences.greek: Τῷ δὲ Σαμουήλ εἶπεν ὁ Κύριος· Ἄκουε τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ λαοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: To the on the other hand Samuel said the Lord: Hear of the voice of the people.
sentences.smooth_english: And the Lord said to Samuel: Listen to the voice of the people.

sentences.greek: Ἦν τότε ἀνὴρ ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, τοὔνομα Κίς, καὶ τούτῳ υἱὸς ὁ Σαούλ, εὐμεγέθης καὶ καλός.
sentences.literal_english: Was then a man out of tribe of Benjamin, the name Kish, and to this one a son the Saul, of good size and beautiful.
sentences.smooth_english: At that time there was a man from the tribe of Benjamin, named Kish, and to him a son, Saul, tall and handsome.

sentences.greek: Ὅ γε Σαούλ πρὸς Σαμουὴλ ἐρωτᾶν ἦλθε· Ποῦ εἰσὶν αἱ ὄνοι τοῦ πατρὸς πλανώμεναι; Ἦν γὰρ τότε Σαμουὴλ ὁ τοῦ λαοῦ προφήτης.
sentences.literal_english: The at least Saul toward Samuel to ask came: Where are the female donkeys of the father wandering? Was for then Samuel the of the people prophet.
sentences.smooth_english: Now Saul came to Samuel to ask: Where are the donkeys of my father that have gone astray? For at that time Samuel was the prophet of the people.

sentences.greek: Καὶ Σαμουήλ· Εὕρηνται αἱ ὄνοι σου, ἔφη, καὶ ἐγώ σε χρίω βασιλέα τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
sentences.literal_english: And Samuel: Have been found the female donkeys of you, he said, and I you anoint king of the Israel.
sentences.smooth_english: And Samuel said: Your donkeys have been found, and I anoint you king of Israel.

sentences.greek: Καὶ πρὸς πάντα τὸν λαόν· Τοῦτον, ἔφη, ἐκλέλεκται ἑαυτῷ Κύριος. Ἐβόησε δὲ ὁ λαός· Ζήτω ὁ βασιλεύς!
sentences.literal_english: And toward all the people: This one, he said, has chosen out for himself Lord. Cried out on the other hand the people: Let live the king!
sentences.smooth_english: And to all the people he said: This one, he said, the Lord has chosen for Himself. And the people shouted: Long live the king!

sentences.greek: Ὁ Σαούλ δικαίως καὶ σωφρόνως πρῶτον μὲν ἦρξε, καὶ ἐταπεινοφρόνει· καὶ ὁ Θεὸς συνέλαβεν αὐτῷ· τὸν γὰρ Νάας ἐνίκησε, τὸν Ἀμμονίτην, τὸν πρέσβεις αὐτοῦ ὑβρίσαντα, ὃς ἐπολιόρκει πόλιν τινὰ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
sentences.literal_english: The Saul justly and prudently first on the one hand ruled, and was humble; and the God helped to him; the for Nahash he conquered, the Ammonite, the ambassadors of him having insulted, who was besieging a city certain of the Israel.
sentences.smooth_english: Saul at first ruled justly and prudently, and was humble; and God helped him; for he defeated Nahash the Ammonite, who had insulted his ambassadors and was besieging a certain city of Israel.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλά, ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα ὁ βασιλεὺς ἠμνημόνευσε τῶν εὐεργετημάτων τοῦ Σαμουήλ, ὧν τὴν ἀρχὴν παρέσχεν αὐτῷ, ὑπὸ Θεοῦ ἀμελεῖται.
sentences.literal_english: But, since most quickly the king was unmindful of the well-doings of the Samuel, of which the beginning he provided to him, by God he is neglected.
sentences.smooth_english: But, as soon as the king forgot the benefits of Samuel, by whom he had been given the rule, he was neglected by God.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ γὰρ Σαμουὴλ ἀπόντος, καὶ μάχης συνάπτεσθαι μελλούσης τοῖς Φιλισταίοις, ὁ Σαούλ ἀνήνεγκεν αὐτὸς τὴν θυσίαν· τῷ δὲ προφήτῃ μόνῳ θέμις ἦν ῥέξαι τὰ ἱερά.
sentences.literal_english: Of the for Samuel being absent, and battle being about to join to the Philistines, the Saul brought up himself the sacrifice; to the on the other hand prophet only right it was to do the sacred things.
sentences.smooth_english: For when Samuel was absent, and a battle was about to be joined with the Philistines, Saul himself offered the sacrifice; but it was lawful only for the prophet to perform the sacred rites.

sentences.greek: Διὰ ταῦτα, ἡ πλείστη τῆς τοῦ Σαούλ στρατιᾶς, πρὶν ἢ μάχην συνάπτειν, τὴν τάξιν ἔλειψεν.
sentences.literal_english: On account of these things, the most of the of Saul army, before or battle to join, the rank left.
sentences.smooth_english: Because of this, most of Saul’s army, before the battle began, left their ranks.

sentences.greek: Ἐν τούτοις τοῖς δεινοῖς, Ἰωνάθαν, ὁ τοῦ Σαούλ, τῷ ἱπποκόμῳ εἶπε· Διαβῶμεν εἰς τὸ τῶν Φιλισταίων στρατόπεδον.
sentences.literal_english: In these the terrible things, Jonathan, the of the Saul, to the groom said: Let us cross into the of the Philistines camp.
sentences.smooth_english: In these dire circumstances, Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to his armor-bearer: Let us cross over to the camp of the Philistines.

sentences.greek: Καί, τοῦ Θεοῦ αὐτοῖς συλλαμβάνοντος, παρέδωκεν αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα τοὺς Φιλισταίους εἰς χεῖρας Ἰσραήλ.
sentences.literal_english: And, of the God to them helping, gave over this the day the Philistines into hands of Israel.
sentences.smooth_english: And, as God helped them, on that day the Philistines were delivered into the hands of Israel.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Σαούλ, τῶν τοῦ Ἀμαλὴκ νενικημένων, τὸ δεύτερον ἠπείθει Θεῷ· τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἀπέστη ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The Saul, of the of Amalek having been conquered, the second time disobeyed to God; the on the other hand spirit of Lord stood away from him.
sentences.smooth_english: Saul, after the defeat of the Amalekites, disobeyed God a second time; and the spirit of the Lord departed from him.

sentences.greek: Οἱ γοῦν Φιλισταῖοι στρατοπεδεύονται ἐπὶ τοῖς ὅροις Ἰσραήλ· συνάγονται δὲ Σαούλ τε καὶ ἄνδρες αὐτοῦ εἰς πόλεμον ἐξ ἐναντίας.
sentences.literal_english: The therefore Philistines encamped upon the borders of Israel; are gathered together on the other hand Saul both and men of him into war from opposite.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore the Philistines encamped on the borders of Israel; and Saul and his men gathered for battle opposite them.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ Γολιάθ, ἀνὴρ Φιλισταῖος, ἑξάπηχυς, ἐκ τῆς παρατάξεως ἐξῆλθεν.
sentences.literal_english: And behold Goliath, man Philistine, six-cubits, out of the battle-line went out.
sentences.smooth_english: And behold, Goliath, a Philistine man, six cubits tall, came out from their ranks.

sentences.greek: Ἔστη μὲν καὶ ἀνεβόησε πρὸς τοὺς Ἰσραήλ· Προκαλέομαι ἐγὼ σήμερον ὑμᾶς εἰς μάχην. Οἱ δὲ Ἰσραηλῖται ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.
sentences.literal_english: He stood on the one hand and cried out toward the Israel: Challenge I today you into battle. The on the other hand Israelites feared exceedingly.
sentences.smooth_english: He stood and shouted to the Israelites: I challenge you today to battle. But the Israelites were greatly afraid.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὁ Δαυίδ, ὁ τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, οὐχ ὑπέμεινε τοῦτο.
sentences.literal_english: But the David, the of the Jesse, not endured this.
sentences.smooth_english: But David, the son of Jesse, did not endure this.

sentences.greek: Προςελθὼν δέ, τῷ Σαούλ· Εἰ θέλεις, ἔφη, πορεύσομαι ἐγώ, ὁ δοῦλός σου, καὶ πρὸς τοῦτον μαχήσομαι.
sentences.literal_english: Having come toward on the other hand, to the Saul: If you wish, he said, will go I, the slave of you, and toward this one will fight.
sentences.smooth_english: He approached Saul and said, If you wish, I, your servant, will go and fight this man.

sentences.greek: Ἠπόρει μὲν ὁ βασιλεύς, βλέπων πρὸς τὴν τοῦ παιδὸς ἡλικίαν. Εἶπε δὲ μέντοι· Ἴθι, καὶ ἔσται Κύριος μετὰ σοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: Was at a loss on the one hand the king, looking toward the of the boy age. He said on the other hand however: Go, and will be Lord with you.
sentences.smooth_english: The king was at a loss, seeing the youth of the boy. Yet he said: Go, and the Lord will be with you.

sentences.greek: Προςῆλθεν οὖν Δαυίδ πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα, καὶ σφενδονήσας, λίθον ἐνέβαλεν εἰς τὸ μέτωπον αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: Went toward therefore David toward the man, and having slung, a stone cast in into the forehead of him.
sentences.smooth_english: So David approached the man, and slinging a stone, he struck it into his forehead.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ δὲ Γολιάθ κειμένου, ἔφυγον οἱ Φιλισταῖοι.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the other hand Goliath lying, fled the Philistines.
sentences.smooth_english: When Goliath fell, the Philistines fled.

groups.group_title: 36. David’s Favor – The Death of Saul.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἰωνάθαν τὸν Δαυίδ ἠγάπησε κατὰ τὴν ψυχὴν αὑτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Jonathan the David loved according to the soul of himself.
sentences.smooth_english: Jonathan loved David as his own soul.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ οὐκ εὐνοϊκῶς ὁ Σαούλ ἔσχε πρὸς Δαυίδ ταύτης τῆς νίκης ἕνεκα, καὶ πολλάκις ἐβουλήθη φονεύειν αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: But not favorably the Saul had toward David of this the victory on account, and often wished to murder him.
sentences.smooth_english: But Saul was not well-disposed toward David because of this victory, and often wished to kill him.

sentences.greek: Διότι ὁ Δαυίδ, τῷ Ἰωνάθαν συμβούλῳ χρώμενος, ἀπῆλθε, καὶ ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν ἐρημίαν· συνήγοντο δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἀδελφοί, καὶ πάντες οἱ πρὸς αὐτὸν εὖ κείμενοι.
sentences.literal_english: Because the David, to the Jonathan as counselor using, went away, and withdrew into the wilderness; were gathered together on the other hand toward him also brothers, and all the ones toward him well lying.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore David, using Jonathan as his adviser, departed and withdrew into the wilderness; and his brothers and all who were well-disposed toward him gathered to him.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν Σαούλ ἐδίωκεν αὐτόν· οὐ μὴν ἀλλά, ὁ Δαυίδ οὐχ ὅπως ἔβλαψε τὸν βασιλέα, ἀλλὰ καὶ δὶς ἔσωσεν αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore Saul was pursuing him; not indeed but, the David not only harmed the king, but also twice saved him.
sentences.smooth_english: So Saul pursued him; yet David not only did no harm to the king, but even saved him twice.

sentences.greek: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, συναθροίζονται Φιλισταῖοι πολεμεῖν τὸν Ἰσραήλ.
sentences.literal_english: In on the other hand the days those, are gathered together Philistines to war the Israel.
sentences.smooth_english: In those days, the Philistines gathered to fight Israel.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐπεὶ εἶδεν ὁ Σαούλ τὴν αὐτῶν παρεμβολήν, ἐφοβήθη.
sentences.literal_english: And when saw the Saul the of them camp, he feared.
sentences.smooth_english: And when Saul saw their camp, he was afraid.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ δὲ πολέμου ἐπὶ Σαούλ βαρύνοντος, ὅδε ἀπέθανεν αὐτός, καὶ οἱ τρεῖς υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ, ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη Γελβωέ.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the other hand war upon Saul being heavy, this one died himself, and the three sons of him, upon the mountains Gilboa.
sentences.smooth_english: As the war pressed heavily upon Saul, he himself died, and his three sons.

sentences.greek: Τὸν Σαούλ ἀποθανόντα ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Δαυίδ, καὶ μάλιστα τὸν Ἰωνάθαν, τὸν προςφιλέστατον.
sentences.literal_english: The Saul having died wept the David, and especially the Jonathan, the most beloved.
sentences.smooth_english: David wept for Saul when he died, and especially for Jonathan, his dearest friend.

sentences.greek: Μετὰ ταῦτα, ἔρχονται πάντες οἱ πρεσβύτεροι Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς τὸν Δαυίδ εἰς Χεβρών, καὶ χρίουσιν αὐτὸν εἰς βασιλέα ἐπὶ πάντα Ἰσραήλ.
sentences.literal_english: After these things, come all the elders of Israel toward the David into Hebron, and anoint him into king upon all Israel.
sentences.smooth_english: After this, all the elders of Israel came to David at Hebron, and anointed him king over all Israel.

sentences.greek: Τὸ μὲν πρῶτον, ὁ βασιλεὺς πρὸς ἅπαντας εἰρήνην ἦγε, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Κύριος ἔπεμψε Ναθὰν τὸν προφήτην, ὃς εἶπεν· Ἔλαβόν σε ἐγὼ ἡγήσασθαι τοῦ λαοῦ μου. Ἔννοιά σοι ἐγένετο οἰκοδομῆσαί μοι ναόν· ὁ δὲ υἱός σου αὐτὸς οἰκοδομήσει.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand first, the king toward all peace led, and toward him the Lord sent Nathan the prophet, who said: Took you I to lead of the people of me. Thought to you became to build to me a temple; the on the other hand son of you himself will build.
sentences.smooth_english: At first, the king lived in peace with everyone, and to him the Lord sent Nathan the prophet, who said: I have chosen you to lead my people. You intended to build me a temple; but your son, he will build it.

sentences.greek: Ὀλίγοις δὲ ἔτεσιν ὕστερον, ἠχαρίστησε διπλῆ τῷ Θεῷ ὁ Δαυίδ διὰ ἀδικίαν. Διπλῆ τε τιμωρίαν τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἔδωκε.
sentences.literal_english: Few on the other hand years later, was ungrateful twofold to the God the David on account of injustice. Twofold both punishment of the sins he gave.
sentences.smooth_english: But a few years later, David greatly offended God through injustice. He received double punishment for his sins.

sentences.greek: Τοῦτο μέν, ὁ Ἀβεσσαλώμ, ὁ τοῦ Δαυίδ, φανερῶς ἀπεστήσατο ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρός· ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς πεζῇ ἐξέφυγεν ἐκ τῆς Ἱεροσολύμης. Ἀλλὰ τὸν Ἀβεσσαλώμ ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἰωὰβ νικηθέντα οἱ σκευοφόροι ἀπέκτειναν.
sentences.literal_english: This on the one hand, the Absalom, the of the David, openly stood away from the father; the on the other hand king on foot fled out of the Jerusalem.
sentences.smooth_english: First, Absalom, David’s son, openly rebelled against his father; and the king fled on foot from Jerusalem. But Absalom, defeated by Joab, was killed by the king’s servants.

sentences.greek: Τοῦτο δέ, τὴν γῆν Ἰσραὴλ ἐπόρθησε λοιμός. Ἀλλὰ ὁ Κύριος, τοῦ Δαυίδ πολλὰ δακρύσαντος, τὸν λαὸν ἐλεημόνως ἔσχεν.
sentences.literal_english: This on the other hand, the land of Israel ravaged a plague. But the Lord, of the David much having wept, the people mercifully had.
sentences.smooth_english: Second, a plague ravaged the land of Israel. But the Lord, after David wept much, mercifully spared the people.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Δαυίδ, τὸν Σολομῶντα, τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, κελεύσας χρίεσθαι εἰς βασιλέα, ἐκοιμήθη μετὰ τῶν πατέρων αὑτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand David, the Solomon, the son of him, having commanded to be anointed into king, fell asleep with the fathers of himself.
sentences.smooth_english: Then David, having ordered that Solomon his son be anointed king, slept with his fathers.

sentences.greek: Ἠγάπησεν ὁ Σολομὼν τὸν Κύριον, πορευόμενος ἐν τοῖς προςτάγμασι Δαυίδ, τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾐτήσατο νοῦν ὀρθόν, ὥςτε διακρίνειν τὸν λαὸν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ.
sentences.literal_english: Loved the Solomon the Lord, journeying in the commands of David, of the father of him, and asked right mind, so as to distinguish the people in righteousness.
sentences.smooth_english: Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the commandments of David his father, and asked for an upright mind, so as to judge the people with justice.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἃ οὐκ ᾐτήσατο, πλοῦτόν τε καὶ δόξαν, ὁ Θεὸς προςέδωκεν αὐτῷ.
sentences.literal_english: And which things not he asked, wealth both and glory, the God added to him.
sentences.smooth_english: And what he did not ask for, both wealth and glory, God also gave him.

sentences.greek: Ὁ γὰρ Σολομὼν ἐβασίλευε πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν, ἕως τῆς γῆς Αἰγύπτου.
sentences.literal_english: The for Solomon was ruling of all the nations, until the land of Egypt.
sentences.smooth_english: For Solomon ruled over all nations as far as the land of Egypt.

sentences.greek: Ἐσωφρόνει ὑπὲρ πάντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ὥςτε τοῦτον γεγονέναι βασιλέα ἐν τοῖς εὐδοκιμωτάτοις.
sentences.literal_english: He was prudent over all the men, so as this one to have become king in the most highly esteemed.
sentences.smooth_english: He was wiser than all men, so that he became one of the most renowned kings.

sentences.greek: Παρεγίνοντο δὲ πάντες ἐκ πάσης χώρας, ἀκοῦσαι τῆς σοφίας τοῦ Σολομῶντος.
sentences.literal_english: Were arriving on the other hand all out of all country, to hear of the wisdom of the Solomon.
sentences.smooth_english: And people came from every land to hear the wisdom of Solomon.

sentences.greek: Ἀπέστειλε γὰρ καὶ ὁ Χιράμ, ὁ βασιλεὺς Τύρου, τοὺς παῖδας αὐτοῦ, ὡς τάχιστα ἤκουσεν ὅτι ὁ Σολομὼν τὸν Δαυίδ πατέρα διεδέξατο.
sentences.literal_english: Sent for also the Hiram, the king of Tyre, the servants of him, as most quickly he heard that the Solomon the David father succeeded.
sentences.smooth_english: For Hiram also, the king of Tyre, sent his servants as soon as he heard that Solomon had succeeded David his father.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ πρὸς ἀλλήλους συμμαχίαν ἐποιήσαντο.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand toward one another alliance made.
sentences.smooth_english: And they made an alliance with each other.

sentences.greek: Ἐβουλεύσατο ὁ Σολομὼν οἰκοδομῆσαι οἶκόν τινα τῷ ὀνόματι Κυρίου Θεοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: Purposed the Solomon to build a house certain to the name of Lord God.
sentences.smooth_english: Solomon planned to build a house for the name of the Lord God.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν εὐθὺς πέμψας πρὸς Χιρὰμ πρέσβεις, ᾔτει· Δοῦλοί σου κοψάτωσάν μοι ξύλα ἐκ τοῦ Λιβάνου.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore straightaway having sent toward Hiram ambassadors, he asked: Slaves of you let cut to me woods out of the Lebanon.
sentences.smooth_english: So he immediately sent ambassadors to Hiram and requested: Let your servants cut wood for me from Lebanon.

sentences.greek: Οὕτως ᾠκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς λίθοις πρότερον ἐξεσμένοις, καὶ κέδροις, καί, ἐν τῷ οἰκοδομεῖσθαι, ψόφος οὐδεὶς ἠκούσθη.
sentences.literal_english: Thus was built the temple with stones formerly having been smoothed, and cedars, and, in the to be built, noise none was heard.
sentences.smooth_english: Thus the temple was built with stones previously hewn, and with cedars, and, during the building, no sound was heard.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Κύριος τότε· Παροικήσω ἐγὼ ἐν μέσῳ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, ἔφη· καὶ οὐδέποτε καταλείψω τὸν λαόν μου.
sentences.literal_english: And the Lord then: Will dwell I in middle of sons of Israel, he said; and never will leave behind the people of me.
sentences.smooth_english: And the Lord then said: I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel, and I will never forsake my people.

sentences.greek: Ἐξεκκλησιάσθησαν μὲν πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα πᾶς ἀνήρ, καὶ ἦραν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὴν κιβωτόν, ἣν εἰςήνεγκαν εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων.
sentences.literal_english: Were gathered into assembly on the one hand toward the king all man, and lifted the priests the ark, which they carried in into the Holy of the holies.
sentences.smooth_english: All the men assembled before the king, and the priests took up the ark, which they brought into the Holy of Holies.

sentences.greek: Ἔπλησε δὲ νέφος τὸν ναόν, καὶ προςεῖπεν ὁ Σολομών, ἀναστὰς πρὸ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου· Κύριε, οὐκ ἔστιν ὡς σὺ Θεὸς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κάτω.
sentences.literal_english: Filled on the other hand a cloud the temple, and addressed the Solomon, having stood up before the altar: Lord, not is as you God in the heaven above and upon the earth below.
sentences.smooth_english: And a cloud filled the temple, and Solomon, standing before the altar, said: Lord, there is none like you, God in heaven above and on the earth beneath.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Σολομὼν ἐβασίλευσεν ἔτη τεσσαράκοντα, καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν ἐν πόλει τοῦ Δαυίδ, τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Solomon ruled years forty, and they buried him in city of the David, of the father of him.
sentences.smooth_english: And Solomon reigned forty years, and they buried him in the city of David his father.

groups.group_title: 40. The Secession of the Tribes. – Rehoboam and Jeroboam. –

sentences.greek: Τῷ δὲ Ἱεροβοάμ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἐφραίμ, προεῤῥήθη ἐκ πολλοῦ ὑπὸ Ἀχιὰ τοῦ προφήτου, ὅτι, τοῦ Σολομῶντος θανόντος, ἄρξοι ἂν αὐτὸς δέκα φυλῶν τῶν Ἰσραήλ· Σολομὼν γάρ, πρὸς τὸ τέλος τῆς βασιλείας ἀφικόμενος, πιστὸς ὢν τῷ Θεῷ οὐ διετέλεσε.
sentences.literal_english: To the on the other hand Jeroboam, out of tribe of Ephraim, it was foretold out of much by Ahijah the prophet, that, of the Solomon having died, might rule he of ten tribes of the Israel; Solomon for, toward the end of the kingdom having arrived, faithful being to the God not continued.
sentences.smooth_english: To Jeroboam, of the tribe of Ephraim, it had long before been foretold by Ahijah the prophet, that, when Solomon died, he himself would rule over ten tribes of Israel; for Solomon, at the end of his reign, did not continue faithful to God.

sentences.greek: Τῷ ὄντι, δέκα φυλαὶ ἐκάλεσαν τὸν Ἱεροβοὰμ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ αὐτὸν βασιλέα ἀνεκήρυξαν.
sentences.literal_english: To the being, ten tribes called the Jeroboam out of Egypt, and him king proclaimed.
sentences.smooth_english: Indeed, ten tribes called Jeroboam out of Egypt and proclaimed him king.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ βασιλεία τούτου τοῦ Ἱεροβοὰμ ἀρχεῖον ἔσχε τὴν πόλιν Σίκιμα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand kingdom of this the Jeroboam seat had the city Shechem.
sentences.smooth_english: The kingdom of this Jeroboam had its capital in the city of Shechem.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μέντοι Ῥοβοάμ, ὁ τοῦ Σολομῶντος, τοῦ πατρὸς ἀποθανόντος, εἰςῆλθεν εἰς Ἱεροσολύμην.
sentences.literal_english: The however Rehoboam, the of the Solomon, of the father having died, entered into Jerusalem.
sentences.smooth_english: But Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, after his father died, entered Jerusalem.

sentences.greek: Ἐκράτησε δὲ ὁ Ῥοβοὰμ μόνον δυοῖν φυλαῖν, Ἰούδα τε καὶ Βενιαμίν.
sentences.literal_english: Conquered on the other hand the Rehoboam only of two tribes, of Judah both and Benjamin.
sentences.smooth_english: Rehoboam retained only two tribes, Judah and Benjamin.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε ὁ Ἱεροβοὰμ ἐποίησε δύο μόσχους χρυσοῦς, καὶ εἶπε πρὸς τὸν λαόν· Παύεσθε ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσολύμην· ἰδοὺ θεοί σου, ὦ Ἰσραήλ!
sentences.literal_english: And then the Jeroboam made two calves golden, and said toward the people: Cease going up into Jerusalem; behold gods of you, O Israel!
sentences.smooth_english: And then Jeroboam made two golden calves, and said to the people: “Cease going up to Jerusalem; behold your gods, O Israel!”

sentences.greek: Τὸν μὲν τῶν μόσχων ἔθετο ἐν Βαιθήλ, τὸν δὲ ἐν Δάν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand of the calves he set in Bethel, the on the other hand in Dan.
sentences.smooth_english: He set one of the calves in Bethel, and the other in Dan.

sentences.greek: Τοῦτό γε φαῦλον πρᾶγμα ἁμαρτίᾳ τε καὶ σκανδάλῳ παρέσχεν ἀφορμήν.
sentences.literal_english: This at least bad thing to sin both and to stumbling-block provided a starting-point.
sentences.smooth_english: This base act gave occasion for sin and scandal.

sentences.greek: Ἀμρὶ δέ, εἷς τῶν τοῦ Ἱεροβοὰμ διαδόχων, ᾠκοδόμησε τὴν Σαμάρειαν, τὴν τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ μητρόπολιν.
sentences.literal_english: Omri on the other hand, one of the of Jeroboam successors, built the Samaria, the of the Israel mother-city.
sentences.smooth_english: Omri, one of Jeroboam’s successors, built Samaria, the capital of Israel.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ Ἀμρὶ τὸ πονηρὸν ἐποίησεν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Κυρίου, καί, πορευθεὶς ἐν πάσῃ τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Ἱεροβοάμ, διὰ τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας αὐτοῦ τὸν Κύριον Θεὸν Ἰσραὴλ ὤργισεν.
sentences.literal_english: But also the Omri the wicked thing did before the Lord, and, having journeyed in all the way of the Jeroboam, on account of the idolatry of him the Lord God of Israel angered.
sentences.smooth_english: But Omri also did evil in the sight of the Lord, and, walking in all the ways of Jeroboam, through his idolatry he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.

sentences.greek: Πάντες οἱ τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ βασιλεῖς, ὀλίγου δεῖν, πονηροὶ ἐγένοντο.
sentences.literal_english: All the of the Israel kings, of little to lack, wicked became.
sentences.smooth_english: Almost all the kings of Israel became wicked.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἀχαάβ, ὁ τοῦ Ἀμρί, ἀσεβὴς ὤν, τὴν Ἰεζάβελ ἔτι ὠμοτέραν ἔγημε.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Ahab, the of the Omri, impious being, the Jezebel still more cruel married.
sentences.smooth_english: Ahab, the son of Omri, being impious, married Jezebel, who was even more cruel.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἀπέστειλεν Ἡλίαν τὸν προφήτην, ὃς προέλεξεν αὐτοῖς ξηρότητα τριετῆ γενήσεσθαι. Λιμὸς γὰρ ἔσχατος ἐν Σαμαρείᾳ ἐγένετο.
sentences.literal_english: And the Lord toward them sent forth Elijah the prophet, who foretold to them dryness three-year to be about to become. Famine for extreme in Samaria became.
sentences.smooth_english: And the Lord sent to them Elijah the prophet, who foretold to them that there would be a drought for three years. For there was a severe famine in Samaria.

sentences.greek: Ἡ μὲν Ἰεζάβελ τὸν θάνατον τῷ Ἡλίᾳ ἠπείλησεν· οὗτος δὲ φοβηθεὶς ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ὅπου ἄγγελός τις αὐτῷ ἐπόρισεν ἐγκρυφίαν καὶ ὀλίγον ὕδατος.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Jezebel the death to the Elijah threatened; this one on the other hand having feared fled into the wilderness, where a messenger certain to him provided a loaf-baked-in-ashes and a little of water.
sentences.smooth_english: Jezebel threatened Elijah with death; but he, being afraid, fled into the desert, where an angel provided him with food and a little water.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὕστερον, ὁ Ἀχαάβ Ναβουθαί τινα, οὗ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐπεθύμει, λιθοβολῆσαι ἐκέλευσε, τῆς Ἰεζάβελ συμβουλευούσης.
sentences.literal_english: But later, the Ahab Naboth a certain, of whom the vineyard he was desiring, to stone he commanded, of the Jezebel advising.
sentences.smooth_english: But later, Ahab, desiring the vineyard of Naboth, ordered him to be stoned, with Jezebel advising him.

sentences.greek: Τοιγαροῦν ὁ Ἡλίας πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα προςῆλθε, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι ἀδίκως ἐφόνευσας Ναβουθαί, ἔνθα ὅπου ἔλειξαν οἱ κύνες τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ, ἐκεῖ λείξουσιν οἱ αὐτοὶ τὸ αἷμά σου, καὶ καταφάγονται τὴν Ἰεζάβελ.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the Elijah toward the king went toward, and said to him: Because unjustly you murdered Naboth, there where licked the dogs the blood of him, there will lick the same ones the blood of you, and will eat up the Jezebel.
sentences.smooth_english: Therefore Elijah came to the king and said to him: “Because you have unjustly killed Naboth, in the place where the dogs licked his blood, there the dogs will lick your blood, and they will devour Jezebel.”

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἀποτετέλεσται ἡ τοῦ προφήτου ἀπειλή.
sentences.literal_english: And has been finished the of the prophet threat.
sentences.smooth_english: And the threat of the prophet was fulfilled.

sentences.greek: Τὸν Ἀχαὰβ πατέρα Ὀχοζίας τότε διεδέξατο, καί, ἕως ἐπὶ Ἰσραὴλ ἐν Σαμαρείᾳ ἐβασίλευσε, τῷ μὲν Βαὰλ προςεκύνησε, καὶ οὕτω τὸν Κύριον παρώργισεν.
sentences.literal_english: The Ahab father Ahaziah then succeeded, and, as long as upon Israel in Samaria he ruled, to the on the one hand Baal he worshipped, and thus the Lord he provoked to anger.
sentences.smooth_english: Ahab, the father of Ahaziah, was succeeded at that time, and while he reigned over Israel in Samaria, he worshipped Baal, and thus angered the Lord.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἡλίας πρὸς βασιλέα ἐπὶ κλίνης κοιμώμενον ἀγγέλους ἀπέστειλε λέξοντας· Ἀπὸ κλίνης οὐ καταβήσῃ, βασιλεῦ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Elijah toward king upon bed sleeping messengers sent forth to say: From bed not will you go down, O king.
sentences.smooth_english: Elijah sent angels to the king, who was lying on his bed, saying: “You shall not come down from your bed, O king.”

sentences.greek: Τοῦ δὲ Ὀχοζίου πεντηκόνταρχόν τινα καὶ πεντήκοντα στρατιώτας κατὰ τοῦ προφήτου ἀποστείλαντος, κατέβη πῦρ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ὃ τὸν πεντηκόνταρχον καὶ τοὺς πεντήκοντα κατέφαγε, καί, κατὰ τὸ τοῦ Ἡλίου ῥῆμα, ἀπέθανεν ὁ βασιλεύς.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the other hand Ahaziah a commander-of-fifty certain and fifty soldiers down from of the prophet having sent forth, went down fire out of heaven, which the commander-of-fifty and the fifty ate up, and, according to the of the Elijah word, died the king.
sentences.smooth_english: When Ahaziah sent a captain of fifty and fifty soldiers against the prophet, fire came down from heaven and consumed the captain and the fifty, and, according to the word of Elijah, the king died.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Ἡλίας, μετὰ ἄλλα τέρατα παντοῖα, εἷλε μαθητὴν τὸν Ἐλισαιέ, καὶ αὐτῷ διέδωκε τὴν δύναμιν τὴν προφητικήν, ἣν καὶ αὐτὸς παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἴληφε.
sentences.literal_english: The Elijah, after other wonders of all sorts, took disciple the Elisha, and to him gave through the power the prophetic, which also himself beside of the God has received.
sentences.smooth_english: Elijah, after performing various other miracles, chose Elisha as his disciple, and gave him the prophetic power which he himself had received from God.

sentences.greek: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα, ἅρμα πυρὸς μεταξὺ ἀμφοτέρων παρενέθετο, καὶ ἀνελήφθη Ἡλίας ὡς ἐν στρόμβῳ.
sentences.literal_english: After on the other hand these things, a chariot of fire between of both was put beside, and was taken up Elijah as in a whirlwind.
sentences.smooth_english: After these things, a chariot of fire came between them, and Elijah was taken up as in a whirlwind.

groups.group_title: 44. The famine and siege of Samaria.

sentences.greek: Χρόνῳ δὲ οὐ πολλῷ ὕστερον, Βεναδάβ, ὁ τῆς Συρίας ὁ βασιλεύς, πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν ἀθροίσας, ἐπολιόρκησε τὴν Σαμάρειαν.
sentences.literal_english: By time on the other hand not much later, Ben-hadad, the of the Syria the king, all the force having gathered, besieged the Samaria.
sentences.smooth_english: Not long after, Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, gathered all his forces and besieged Samaria.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐν Σαμαρείᾳ, ὥςτε κεφαλὴν ὄνου πεντήκοντα ἀργυρίου πωλεῖσθαι.
sentences.literal_english: And became a famine great in Samaria, so as a head of a donkey for fifty of silver to be sold.
sentences.smooth_english: And there was a great famine in Samaria, so that the head of a donkey was sold for fifty silver coins.

sentences.greek: Τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, Ἰωράμ, πρῶτον ἐβουλήθη τὸν Ἐλισαιὲ ἀναιρεῖν, τῶν κακῶν αἰτίαν, ὡς ᾤετο.
sentences.literal_english: Then the king of the Israel, Jehoram, first wished the Elisha to destroy, of the evils cause, as he was supposing.
sentences.smooth_english: Then the king of Israel, Joram, first wished to kill Elisha, whom he considered the cause of the calamities.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ἐλισαιὲ εἶπεν· Αὔριον, τῇ αὐτῇ ὥρᾳ, μέτρον σιλίγνεως πωληθήσεται σίγλου ἑνός.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Elisha said: Tomorrow, to the same hour, a measure of fine wheat flour will be sold of a shekel one.
sentences.smooth_english: But Elisha said: “Tomorrow, at this same hour, a measure of fine flour will be sold for one shekel.”

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὄντως, τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ, οἱ πολέμιοι ᾠήθησαν διὰ νυκτὸς ἀκοῦσαι ταραχὴν ἁρμάτων, καὶ ἵππων, καὶ δυνάμεως μεγάλης· ἀπέδρασαν οὖν φοβηθέντες, ἐγκαταλειφθείσης πάσης τῆς ἀποσκευῆς.
sentences.literal_english: And truly, to the next day, the enemies supposed through of night to hear a disturbance of chariots, and of horses, and of a force great; they ran away therefore having feared, having been left behind of all the baggage.
sentences.smooth_english: And indeed, the next day, the enemies thought they heard during the night the noise of chariots, horses, and a great force; so they fled in fear, leaving behind all their baggage.

sentences.greek: Οὕτως ἀποτετέλεσται ὁ λόγος Ἐλισαιέ.
sentences.literal_english: Thus has been finished the word of Elisha.
sentences.smooth_english: Thus the word of Elisha was fulfilled.

sentences.greek: Κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν χρόνον, Γοθολία, ἡ τοῦ Ἀχαὰβ καὶ τῆς Ἰεζάβελ, καίπερ ἀσεβὴς εἰς τὸν Θεόν, τῷ Ἰούδα βασιλεῖ Ἰωρὰμ ἐγαμήσατο.
sentences.literal_english: According to the same time, Athaliah, the of the Ahab and of the Jezebel, although impious into the God, to the of Judah king Jehoram married.
sentences.smooth_english: At the same time, Athaliah, daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, although impious toward God, married Joram, king of Judah.

sentences.greek: Τοῦ δὲ υἱοῦ αὐτῆς Ὀχοζίου τελευτήσαντος, ἀπέσφαξε πάντας τοὺς ἐκ τοῦ βασιλείου γένους ὄντας, πλὴν τὸν Ἰώαν, ὃς ἐκρύβη ἀπὸ τοῦ προςώπου Γοθολίας, καὶ οὐκ ἐθανατώθη.
sentences.literal_english: Of the on the other hand son of her Ahaziah having died, she slaughtered all the ones out of the royal race being, except the Joash, who was hidden from the face of Athaliah, and not was put to death.
sentences.smooth_english: When her son Ahaziah died, she slaughtered all those of royal descent, except for Joash, who was hidden from the sight of Athaliah and was not killed.

sentences.greek: Ἰώας μὲν οὕτως ἔλαθεν, ἐν οἴκῳ Κυρίου, μεταξὺ τῆς Γοθολίας πάντος τοῦ Ἰούδα μοναρχούσης.
sentences.literal_english: Joash on the one hand thus escaped notice, in house of Lord, meanwhile of the Athaliah of all the Judah being sole ruler.
sentences.smooth_english: Thus Joash escaped, in the house of the Lord, while Athaliah ruled as sole monarch over all Judah.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ Γοθολία τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Κυρίου διαρπάσαι ἔδωκε τοῖς στρατιώταις, καὶ τοῖς τοῦ ναοῦ χρήμασι τὸν Βαάλ ἐκόσμησεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Athaliah the house of the Lord to plunder gave to the soldiers, and to the of the temple things the Baal adorned.
sentences.smooth_english: Athaliah gave the soldiers permission to plunder the house of the Lord, and with the treasures of the temple she adorned the temple of Baal.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ πλησίον ἤδη βασίλισσα ἐγένετο τοῦ τιμωρίαν διδόναι τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων σύμμετρον.
sentences.literal_english: But near already queen became of the punishment to give of the sins commensurate.
sentences.smooth_english: But the queen was already near the time to receive fitting punishment for her sins.

sentences.greek: Τῷ δὲ ἔτει τῷ ἑβδόμῳ τῆς Γοθολίας βασιλευούσης, ἔδειξεν Ἰωδαὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς τῷ λαῷ τὸν τοῦ Ὀχοζίου υἱόν· καὶ ὁ Ἰώας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ἀνεκηρύχθη βασιλεύς.
sentences.literal_english: In the on the other hand year the seventh of the Athaliah ruling, showed Jehoiada the high priest to the people the of the Ahaziah son; and the Joash in the temple was proclaimed king.
sentences.smooth_english: In the seventh year of Athaliah’s reign, Jehoiada the high priest revealed to the people the son of Ahaziah; and Joash was proclaimed king in the temple.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ἡ Γοθολία τότε ἀκούσασα τὴν φωνὴν τῶν τρεχόντων, καὶ αὕτη εἰςῆλθεν εἰς τὸν ναόν· καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν βασιλέα εἰς θρόνον ἐγκαθίζοντα, διέῤῥηξε τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐβόησε· Προδοσία, προδοσία!
sentences.literal_english: But the Athaliah then having heard the voice of the ones running, also this one entered into the temple; and having seen the king into throne sitting in, she tore through the garments of her, and cried out: Treason, treason!
sentences.smooth_english: But when Athaliah heard the sound of those running, she too entered the temple; and seeing the king sitting on the throne, she tore her clothes and cried out, “Treason, treason!”

sentences.greek: Ἀπήγαγον δὲ αὐτὴν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ, καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.
sentences.literal_english: They led away on the other hand her out of the temple, and killed.
sentences.smooth_english: They led her out of the temple and killed her.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε εἰςελθὼν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς εἰς οἶκον τοῦ Βαάλ, τὰ θυσιαστήρια καὶ τὰς εἰκόνας αὐτοῦ συνέτριψαν.
sentences.literal_english: And then having entered all the people into house of the Baal, the altars and the images of him shattered together.
sentences.smooth_english: Then all the people entered the house of Baal and smashed his altars and images.

sentences.greek: Πάντας μὲν ἀνθρώπους ἀρετῇ Ἰώας ὑπερέβαλεν, Ἰωδαὲ τοῦ ἱερέως ἔτι ζῶντος· ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἀπέθανεν, εἰς πᾶσαν κακίαν ὁ Ἰώας κατέπεσεν.
sentences.literal_english: All on the one hand men in virtue Joash surpassed, of Jehoiada the priest still living; since on the other hand he died, into all wickedness the Joash fell down.
sentences.smooth_english: Joash surpassed all men in virtue while Jehoiada the priest was still alive; but after he died, Joash fell into every kind of wickedness.

groups.group_title: 47. Hoshea, last king of Israel. – The ten tribes in Assyria.

sentences.greek: Ὠσηέ, τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ βασιλεύς, τὴν ἀδικίαν ἠδίκησεν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ πρῶτον μὲν δοῦλος ἐγενήθη τῷ Σαλμανασσάρ, τῶν Ἀσσυρίων βασιλεῖ.
sentences.literal_english: Hoshea, of the Israel king, the injustice did unjustly in eyes of the Lord, and first on the one hand slave became to the Shalmaneser, to the of Assyrians king.
sentences.smooth_english: Hoshea, king of Israel, did evil in the sight of the Lord, and first became a servant to Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians.

sentences.greek: Τῷ δὲ ἐννάτῳ ἔτει τοῦ Ὠσηὲ βασιλεύοντος, ὁ Σαλμανασσάρ, τὴν Σαμάρειαν καταλαβών, τὸν Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὴν Ἀσσυρίαν ἀπῴκισε.
sentences.literal_english: In the on the other hand ninth year of the Hoshea ruling, the Shalmaneser, the Samaria having taken down, the Israel into the Assyria settled away.
sentences.smooth_english: In the ninth year of Hoshea’s reign, Shalmaneser captured Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ταῦτα, διότι ἥμαρτον οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸν Κύριον, τὸν Θεὸν αὐτῶν, τὸν ἀναγαγόντα αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῆς γῆς Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ὅτι προςεκύνησαν θεοὺς ξένους.
sentences.literal_english: And became these things, because sinned the sons of Israel into the Lord, the God of them, the having led up them out of the land of Egypt, and because they worshipped gods foreign.
sentences.smooth_english: And these things happened because the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord, their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, and because they worshipped foreign gods.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος μέντοι αὐτοῖς συνεβεβουλεύκει διὰ τὴν τῶν προφητῶν φωνήν, λεγόντων· Ἀποστράφητε ἀπὸ τῶν ὁδῶν τῶν πονηρῶν ὑμῶν, καὶ φυλάξατε τὰς ἐντολάς μου καὶ τὰς λειτουργίας.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Lord however to them had counseled together through the of the prophets voice, saying: Turn away from the ways the wicked of you, and guard the commandments of me and the services.
sentences.smooth_english: But the Lord nevertheless advised them through the voice of the prophets, saying: Turn away from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and ordinances.

sentences.greek: Ὡς οὖν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ Κυρίου, ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν αὐτοὺς εἰς χεῖρας διαρπαζόντων αὐτούς, καὶ ἀπέῤῥιψεν ἀπὸ προςώπου.
sentences.literal_english: As therefore not they heard of the Lord, the Lord gave them into hands of ones plundering them, and threw away from face.
sentences.smooth_english: Since they did not listen to the Lord, the Lord gave them into the hands of those who plundered them, and cast them away from His presence.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Τωβίας, ὁ πρεσβύτερος, ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Νεφθαλί, ἐν ταῖς τοῦ Σαλμανασσὰρ ἡμέραις, ᾐχμαλωτεύθη· οὐ μέντοι κατέλειψε τὴν ὁδόν, τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Tobit, the elder, out of the tribe Naphtali, in the of the Shalmaneser days, was taken captive; not however he left down the way, the of the Lord.
sentences.smooth_english: Tobias the elder, from the tribe of Naphtali, was taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser; yet he did not forsake the way of the Lord.

sentences.greek: Ἔλαβε δὲ Ἄνναν γυναῖκα ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς ἑαυτοῦ, ἣ υἱὸν ἔτεκεν αὐτῷ, τοὔνομα Τωβίαν· τὸ δὲ παιδίον τῷ Θεῷ λατρεύειν ἐπαιδεύθη.
sentences.literal_english: He took on the other hand Anna woman out of the tribe of himself, who a son bore to him, the name Tobias; the on the other hand child to the God to serve was educated.
sentences.smooth_english: He took Anna as his wife from his own tribe, and she bore him a son, named Tobias; and the child was raised to serve God.

sentences.greek: Καί, ὅτε πάντες μὲν οἱ ἐκ τοῦ γένους Τωβίου ἐκ τῶν κρεῶν τῷ νόμῳ ἀπαγορευθέντων ἤσθιον, ὅδε ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ τῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ προςταγμάτων ἐμέμνητο.
sentences.literal_english: And, when all on the one hand the ones out of the race of Tobit out of the meats to the law having been forbidden were eating, this one in the soul of the of the God commands had remembered.
sentences.smooth_english: And when all the people of Tobias’s lineage ate meats forbidden by the Law, he remembered in his soul the commandments of God.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἅμα ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Νινευὴ μετά τε τῆς γυναικὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ, ἐπείθετο τῷ Θεῷ· ὁ δὲ Ὕψιστος ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Σαλμανασσὰρ βασιλέως, ὅτι ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς διένεμε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, τοῖς αἰχμαλώτοις.
sentences.literal_english: And at the same time of having come of him into Nineveh with both of the wife and of the son, he was obeying to the God; the on the other hand Highest gave to him favor before of the Shalmaneser king, because alms many he distributed to the brothers of him, to the captives.
sentences.smooth_english: And when he came to Nineveh with his wife and son, he obeyed God; and the Most High gave him favor before King Shalmaneser, because he distributed many alms to his brothers, the captives.

sentences.greek: Ἐπορεύετο μὲν ὁ Τωβίας εἰς Ῥάγους τῆς Μηδίας· καὶ λαβὼν ἀργυρίου τάλαντα δέκα, ἃ παρὰ τοῦ Σαλμανασσὰρ ἐδέξατο δῶρα, ταῦτα ἔχρησεν ἀνθρώπῳ τινὶ πενεστάτῳ, Γαβαήλῳ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Νεφθαλί.
sentences.literal_english: Was journeying on the one hand the Tobit into Rages of the Media; and having taken of silver talents ten, which beside of the Shalmaneser he received gifts, these things he lent to man a certain poorest, Gabael out of the tribe of Naphtali.
sentences.smooth_english: Tobias traveled to Rages of Media; and having received ten talents of silver, which he had accepted as gifts from Shalmaneser, he lent them to a certain very poor man, Gabael, from the tribe of Naphtali.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Γαβάηλος τοῦτο τὸ δάνεισμα χειρογράφῳ ὡμολόγησεν.
sentences.literal_english: And the Gabael this the loan by handwritten note acknowledged.
sentences.smooth_english: And Gabael acknowledged this loan with a written agreement.

sentences.greek: Ὡς συντόμως εἰπεῖν, τέλος τοῦ βίου τὴν εὐεργεσίαν ἐποιήσατο ὁ Τωβίας.
sentences.literal_english: As concisely to say, goal of the life the well-doing made the Tobit.
sentences.smooth_english: In short, Tobias performed acts of kindness until the end of his life.

sentences.greek: Εἰ γάρ τινα ἐκ τοῦ γένους αὑτοῦ ἐθεώρει ἀποροῦντα, ἄρτους ἢ ἱμάτια ἐδίδω αὐτῷ, κατὰ τὴν δύναμιν.
sentences.literal_english: If for a certain one out of the race of himself he was observing being at a loss, breads or garments he was giving to him, according to the power.
sentences.smooth_english: For if he saw anyone of his own people in need, he would give him bread or clothing, according to his ability.

sentences.greek: Καὶ εἴ τινα ἀπέκτεινε Σενναχηρὶμ ὁ βασιλεύς, ὁ τοῦ Σαλμανασσὰρ διάδοχος, ὅδε ἔθαψεν αὐτόν.
sentences.literal_english: And if a certain one killed Sennacherib the king, the of the Shalmaneser successor, this one buried him.
sentences.smooth_english: And if Sennacherib the king, the successor of Shalmaneser, killed anyone, this man would bury him.

groups.group_title: 50. Tobias deprived of all good things.

sentences.greek: Πορευθεὶς δὲ εἷς τῶν ἐν Νινευῇ, ὑπέδειξε τῷ βασιλεῖ περὶ Τωβίου, ὅτι τοὺς τεθνηκότας θάπτει.
sentences.literal_english: Having journeyed on the other hand one of the ones in Nineveh, pointed under to the king about of Tobit, that the having died he buries.
sentences.smooth_english: But one of the people in Nineveh went and informed the king about Tobit, that he was burying the dead.

sentences.greek: Τωβίας οὖν, πάντων τῶν χρημάτων ἀποστερηθείς, ἔφυγεν, οὐδὲν ἔχων πλὴν Ἄνναν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν υἱόν· καὶ ἔλαθε τὸν βασιλέα.
sentences.literal_english: Tobit therefore, of all the possessions having been deprived, fled, nothing having except Anna the wife of him and the son; and escaped notice the king.
sentences.smooth_english: So Tobit, deprived of all his possessions, fled, having nothing except Anna his wife and his son; and he escaped the notice of the king.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ πλησίον ἔψεγον αὐτόν, λέγοντες· Οὐκοῦν φοβῇ φονευθῆναι περὶ τούτου;
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand near blamed him, saying: Therefore not you fear to be murdered about of this?
sentences.smooth_english: But those nearby reproached him, saying: Are you not afraid to be killed for this?

sentences.greek: Οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ ὁ Τωβίας τὸν Θεὸν πάσῃ θεραπείᾳ ἐθεράπευεν.
sentences.literal_english: Not indeed but the Tobit the God with all service was serving.
sentences.smooth_english: Nevertheless, Tobias served God with all devotion.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ἐπειδὴ τὸν βασιλέα ἀπέκτειναν οἱ δύο υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ, ὁ Τωβίας τὴν πρότερον ἕξιν ἀνέλαβε, καὶ τὸν οἶκον.
sentences.literal_english: But since the king killed the two sons of him, the Tobit the former state took up, and the house.
sentences.smooth_english: But when the king was killed by his two sons, Tobit resumed his former way of life, and his household.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐν ὑστέρῳ οὐκ ἐπαύσατο εὖ ποιῶν πάντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους.
sentences.literal_english: And in later not he ceased well doing all the men.
sentences.smooth_english: And afterwards he did not cease doing good to all people.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Κύριος μέντοι, ἵνα δοκιμάζῃ τὸν Τωβίαν, τῆς ὄψεως αὐτὸν ἐστέρησε, παράδειγμα τοῖς ἀπογόνοις αὐτὸν καθιστάς.
sentences.literal_english: The Lord however, in order that he might test the Tobit, of the sight him deprived, an example to the descendants him setting down.
sentences.smooth_english: However, the Lord, in order to test Tobit, deprived him of his sight, making him an example for his descendants.

sentences.greek: Τοῦτο μὲν δὴ ὁ γέρων καρτερικῶς ὑπέμεινε, λέγων· Ἡμεῖς πάντες τῶν ἁγίων υἱοί· τοῦτον τὸν βίον ἐλπίζομεν, ὃν τοῖς οὐ καταλιποῦσιν αὐτὸν δώσει ὁ Θεός.
sentences.literal_english: This on the one hand indeed the old man patiently endured, saying: We all of the holy ones sons; this the life we hope for, which to the ones not having left down him will give the God.
sentences.smooth_english: The old man endured this patiently, saying: We are all children of the saints; we hope for that life which God will give to those who do not abandon him.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ εἶπε· Ποῦ εἰσὶν αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου, καὶ αἱ δικαιοσύναι σου;
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand wife of him said: Where are the alms of you, and the righteousnesses of you?
sentences.smooth_english: But his wife said: Where are your acts of charity and your righteousness?

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ ὁ Τωβίας· Ὦ Κύριε, ἔφη, δίκαιος εἶ, μνήσθητί μου, καὶ ἐπίβλεψον ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ.
sentences.literal_english: But the Tobit: O Lord, he said, righteous you are, remember of me, and look upon upon me.
sentences.smooth_english: But Tobit said: O Lord, he said, you are righteous, remember me, and look upon me.

groups.group_title: 52. Tobias gives good advice to his son.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Τωβίας, νομίσας πλησίον γίνεσθαι τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν, τὸν υἱὸν ἐκάλεσεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Tobit, having supposed near to become of the to die, the son called.
sentences.smooth_english: Tobias, thinking that his death was near, called his son.

sentences.greek: Ὦ παῖ, ἔφη, τίμα τὴν μητέρα σου πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς σου· μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς τὸ πρόςωπόν σου ἀπὸ παντὸς πτωχοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: O boy, he said, honor the mother of you all the days of the life of you; not turn away the face of you from every poor.
sentences.smooth_english: “My child,” he said, “honor your mother all the days of your life; do not turn your face away from any poor person.

sentences.greek: Ἐὰν ὀλίγον σοι ὑπάρχῃ, κατὰ τὸ ὀλίγον μὴ φοβοῦ ποιεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην.
sentences.literal_english: If a little to you belongs, according to the little not fear to do alms.
sentences.smooth_english: If you have little, do not be afraid to give alms according to what you have.

sentences.greek: Μισθὸν γὰρ ἀγαθὸν θησαυρίζεις σεαυτῷ εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν ἀνάγκης.
sentences.literal_english: Reward for good you treasure up to yourself into the day of necessity.
sentences.smooth_english: For you are storing up a good reward for yourself for the day of need.

sentences.greek: Καὶ μὴ φοβοῦ, παιδίον, ὅτι πτωχοὶ ἐσμέν· ὑπάρξει γὰρ σοι πολλά, ἐὰν φοβηθῇς τὸν Θεόν, καὶ ποιήσῃς τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
sentences.literal_english: And not fear, child, because poor we are; will belong for to you many things, if you should fear the God, and should do the good before him.
sentences.smooth_english: And do not be afraid, child, that we are poor; for many things will be yours if you fear God and do what is good before Him.

sentences.greek: Πολλὰ δὲ καὶ ἄλλα βέλτιστα συνεβούλευσεν αὐτῷ, καὶ πορεύεσθαι ἐνέτειλεν, ὡς λαβεῖν τὰ δέκα τάλαντα ἀργυρίου, ἃ ἔχρησε τῷ Γαβαήλῳ.
sentences.literal_english: Many on the other hand and other best things he advised to him, and to journey he enjoined, as to take the ten talents of silver, which he lent to the Gabael.
sentences.smooth_english: He also gave him much other excellent advice, and ordered him to go to receive the ten talents of silver which he had deposited with Gabael.

groups.group_title: 53. The journey of the younger Tobias.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Τωβίας ὁ νεώτερος, ζητήσας ἄνθρωπόν τινα συμπορευσόμενον, ἐπέτυχε νεανίᾳ, ὃν οὐκ ᾔδει εἶναι τὸν ἄγγελον Ῥαφαήλ.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Tobias the younger, having sought a man certain about to journey together, met a youth, whom not he knew to be the messenger Raphael.
sentences.smooth_english: The younger Tobias, seeking someone to accompany him, met a young man, whom he did not know was the angel Raphael.

sentences.greek: Καὶ πορευόμενοι εὐθύς, εἰς Ῥάγους ἀμφότεροι ἀφίκοντο.
sentences.literal_english: And journeying straightaway, into Rages both arrived.
sentences.smooth_english: And traveling together, both arrived at Rages.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ ἄγγελος πρὸς Τωβίαν· Σήμερον, εἶπεν, αὐλισθησόμεθα παρὰ Ῥαγουήλ· αὐτὸς γὰρ συγγενής σου ἐστί.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand messenger toward Tobias: Today, he said, we will lodge beside Raguel; he for a relative of you is.
sentences.smooth_english: The angel said to Tobias, “Today we will lodge with Raguel; for he is your relative.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἐστὶν αὐτῷ θυγάτηρ, ὀνόματι Σάῤῥα, ἣν παρὰ πατρὸς αἰτήσεις, καὶ εἰς γυναῖκα ἕξεις.
sentences.literal_english: And is to him a daughter, to name Sarah, whom beside father you will ask, and into wife you will have.
sentences.smooth_english: He has a daughter named Sarah, whom you will ask from her father, and she will be your wife.

sentences.greek: Πᾶσα ἡ κληρονομία αὐτῆς περιγενήσεταί σοι, διότι σὺ μόνος εἶ ἐκ τοῦ γένους αὐτῆς· λαλήσω ἐγὼ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτῆς.
sentences.literal_english: All the inheritance of her will come around to you, because you alone are out of the race of her; will speak I to the father of her.
sentences.smooth_english: All her inheritance will come to you, for you alone are of her family; I will speak to her father.”

groups.group_title: 54. The marriage of the younger Tobias.

sentences.greek: Καὶ Τωβίας τὸ προςτεταγμένον ἐποίησεν.
sentences.literal_english: And Tobias the having been enjoined did.
sentences.smooth_english: And Tobias did as he was commanded.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν ὁ Ῥαγουὴλ λαβὼν τῆς χειρὸς τὴν θυγατέρα αὑτοῦ, παρέδωκεν αὐτὴν Τωβίᾳ γυναῖκα, καὶ εἶπεν· Ὁ Κύριος, ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ Ἀβραάμ, καὶ τοῦ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τοῦ Ἰακὼβ ὑμῖν δῷ χάριν.
sentences.literal_english: Therefore the Raguel having taken of the hand the daughter of himself, gave over her to Tobias wife, and said: The Lord, the God of the Abraham, and of the Isaac and of the Jacob to you may give favor.
sentences.smooth_english: So Raguel, taking his daughter by the hand, gave her to Tobias as his wife, and said, “May the Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, grant you grace.”

sentences.greek: Ἐν δὲ τῷ Τωβίαν καὶ Σάῤῥαν συντελεῖν τὸν γάμον αὐτῶν, ὁ ἄγγελος, ὁ Ῥαφαήλ, λαβὼν παῖδα ἕνα καὶ δύο καμήλους, ἐπορεύθη μόνος εἰς Ῥάγους τῆς Μηδίας πρὸς τὸν Γαβάηλον.
sentences.literal_english: In on the other hand the Tobias and Sarah to complete the marriage of them, the messenger, the Raphael, having taken slave one and two camels, journeyed alone into Rages of the Media toward the Gabael.
sentences.smooth_english: While Tobias and Sarah were completing their marriage, the angel Raphael, taking a servant and two camels, went alone to Rages of Media to Gabael.

sentences.greek: Καὶ αὐτόν, ἀποδόντα τὰ δέκα τάλαντα, ἤγαγε πρὸς τὸν Τωβίαν τὸν νεώτερον.
sentences.literal_english: And him, having given back the ten talents, led toward the Tobias the younger.
sentences.smooth_english: And after Gabael had returned the ten talents, he brought him to the younger Tobias.

sentences.greek: Ἦδη γὰρ ὁ Τωβίας ὁ νεώτερος, σὺν ἑαυτῷ διανοούμενος, ἔλεγεν· Ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ μου ἀριθμοῦσι τὰς ἡμέρας.
sentences.literal_english: Already for the Tobias the younger, with to himself pondering, was saying: The father and the mother of me number the days.
sentences.smooth_english: For already the younger Tobias, reflecting to himself, was saying: My father and my mother are counting the days.

groups.group_title: 55. The return of the younger Tobias.

sentences.greek: Μετὰ ταῦτα, ἐπορεύοντο μὲν οἴκαδε Τωβίας τε καὶ Ῥαφαήλ· ὁ δὲ πατὴρ Τωβίου ἐξήρχετο πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἐπ᾿ οἰκέτην ἐπιστηριζόμενος, τῷ υἱῷ ὑπήντησε.
sentences.literal_english: After these things, were journeying on the one hand homeward Tobias both and Raphael; the on the other hand father of Tobias was going out toward the door, and upon a household-servant leaning, to the son met.
sentences.smooth_english: After these things, Tobias and Raphael were on their way home; and the father of Tobias came out to the door, and leaning on a servant, met his son.

sentences.greek: Προςδραμοῦσα δὲ Ἄννα, ἣ καθ᾿ ἡμέραν προςέβλεπε τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπῃ ὁ υἱὸς ἂν ἐπανέρχοιτο, ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτῆς, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἶδόν σε, παιδίον· ἀσμένως ἐγὼ ἀποθανοῦμαι.
sentences.literal_english: Having run toward on the other hand Anna, who according to day was looking toward the way where the son might return, fell upon upon the neck of the son of her, and said to him: I saw you, child; gladly I will die.
sentences.smooth_english: And Anna, who every day looked toward the road by which her son might return, ran forward and fell upon the neck of her son, and said to him: I have seen you, my child; now I can die gladly.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ νεανίας ἀσπασάμενος τοὺς γονεῖς, ἤλειψε τῇ ἰχθύος τινὸς χολῇ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ πατρός, ὃς ἀνέβλεψε παραχρῆμα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand youth having greeted the parents, smeared with the of fish a certain gall the eyes of the father, who saw again immediately.
sentences.smooth_english: The young man, after greeting his parents, anointed his father's eyes with the gall of a certain fish, and he immediately regained his sight.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε τῷ πατρὶ διεξῆλθε πάντα τὰ γενόμενα αὑτῷ ἐν τῇ Μηδίᾳ.
sentences.literal_english: And then to the father went through all the things having become to him in the Media.
sentences.smooth_english: And then he recounted to his father all that had happened to him in Media.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Ῥαφαὴλ ἐξεδήλωσεν ἑαυτὸν ὄντα ἄγγελον, ἠφανίσθη, καὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τὸν πέμψαντα ἐπανῆλθεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Raphael having shown forth himself being a messenger, was made invisible, and toward the God the having sent returned.
sentences.smooth_english: And Raphael revealed himself to be an angel, disappeared, and returned to God who had sent him.

sentences.greek: Κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν χρόνον, ὁ Ἐζεχίας, ὁ τοῦ Ἄχαζ, ἐβασίλευε τοῦ Ἰούδα, καὶ τὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐντολὰς ἐτέλει ἀκριβῶς.
sentences.literal_english: According to the same time, the Hezekiah, the of the Ahaz, was ruling of the Judah, and the of the God commandments was completing accurately.
sentences.smooth_english: At the same time, Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, was reigning over Judah, and he kept the commandments of God precisely.

sentences.greek: Ἐν τῷ Κυρίῳ ἤλπισε, καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτόν, καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐγενήθη ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐν βασιλεῦσιν Ἰούδα.
sentences.literal_english: In the Lord he hoped, and after him, and before him not became like to him in kings of Judah.
sentences.smooth_english: He trusted in the Lord, and after him, and before him, there was none like him among the kings of Judah.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἀσσυρίων, Σενναχηρίμ, μεγάλην στρατιὰν συνελέξατο· τότε μὲν ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὰς πόλεις Ἰούδα, καὶ συνέλαβεν αὐτάς· τότε δὲ πρὸς Ἐζεχίαν ἔπεμψε τὸν Ῥαψάκην.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand king of the Assyrians, Sennacherib, a great army gathered together; then on the one hand went up upon the cities of Judah, and captured them; then on the other hand toward Hezekiah sent the Rabshakeh.
sentences.smooth_english: Now the king of the Assyrians, Sennacherib, gathered a great army; then he went up against the cities of Judah and captured them; then he sent Rabshakeh to Hezekiah.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ὁ Ῥαψάκης, ἐναντίον τοῦ παντὸς λαοῦ, μέγιστα ἀπειλήσας, εἶπεν· Ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως τῶν Ἀσσυρίων. Οὔτε γὰρ ὁ Ἐζεχίας, οὔτε ὁ Κύριος αὐτοῦ ἐξαιρήσει, οὐ μὴ παραδοθῇ ἡ πόλις Ἱεροσολύμη ἐν χειρὶ Σενναχηρίμ.
sentences.literal_english: And the Rabshakeh, opposite of the all people, greatest things having threatened, said: Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians. Neither for the Hezekiah, neither the Lord of him will take out, not not may be given over the city Jerusalem in hand of Sennacherib.
sentences.smooth_english: And Rabshakeh, before all the people, having threatened greatly, said: Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians. For neither Hezekiah nor his Lord will deliver you; the city of Jerusalem will surely be handed over into the hand of Sennacherib.

groups.group_title: 57. Sennacherib defeated in a great battle.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν Ἐζεχίας, ὡς ἤκουσε τοῦτο, διέῤῥηξε τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, καί, εἰςελθὼν εἰς οἶκον τοῦ Κυρίου, λέγει· Κύριε, σῶσον ἡμᾶς ἐκ χειρὸς τούτου τοῦ βασιλέως.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Hezekiah, as he heard this, tore through the garments of him, and, having entered into house of the Lord, says: Lord, save us out of hand of this the king.
sentences.smooth_english: When Hezekiah heard this, he tore his garments, and, entering the house of the Lord, said: Lord, save us from the hand of this king.

sentences.greek: Τοῖς δὲ παρὰ τοῦ Ἐζεχίου ἐλθοῦσιν Ἡσαΐας, ὁ προφήτης, ἀπεκρίνατο· Τάδε ἀγγέλλετε πρὸς τὸν κύριον ὑμῶν· Τάδε λέγει Κύριος ὁ Θεός· Ὁ τῶν Ἀσσυρίων βασιλεὺς οὔτε ἐξελεύσεται, οὔτε βέλος τοξεύσει εἰς τὴν πόλιν ταύτην. Τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἦλθεν, ἀποστρέψει ὁ Σενναχηρίμ.
sentences.literal_english: To the on the other hand beside of the Hezekiah having come Isaiah, the prophet, answered: These things announce toward the lord of you; These things says Lord the God: The of the Assyrians king neither will go out, neither arrow will shoot into the city this. To the way to which he came, will turn away the Sennacherib.
sentences.smooth_english: To those who came from Hezekiah, Isaiah the prophet replied: Announce this to your lord: Thus says the Lord God: The king of the Assyrians will neither come out nor shoot an arrow into this city. By the way he came, Sennacherib will return.

sentences.greek: Τότε εἰσῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ Κυρίου εἰς τὴν τῶν Ἀσσυρίων παρεμβολήν, καὶ ἑκατὸν ὀγδοηκονταπέντε χιλιάδας ἐκεῖ ἐπάταξεν.
sentences.literal_english: Then entered the messenger of the Lord into the of the Assyrians camp, and a hundred eighty-five thousands there struck.
sentences.smooth_english: Then the angel of the Lord entered the camp of the Assyrians and struck down one hundred eighty-five thousand there.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ Σενναχηρίμ, ὅτε τοσούτους εἶδε νεκρούς, ἀπέστρεψε παραχρῆμα.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Sennacherib, when so many he saw corpses, turned away immediately.
sentences.smooth_english: When Sennacherib saw so many dead, he immediately withdrew.

sentences.greek: Οὕτως ὁ Θεὸς τῇδε τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἔσωσε τὸν Ἐζεχίαν.
sentences.literal_english: Thus the God to this the day saved the Hezekiah.
sentences.smooth_english: Thus God saved Hezekiah on this day.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Ἐζεχίας τῆς βασιλείας διάδοχον ἔσχεν υἱὸν κάκιστον, τοὔνομα Μανασσῆ.
sentences.literal_english: The Hezekiah of the kingdom successor had a son worst, the name Manasseh.
sentences.smooth_english: Hezekiah had as successor to the kingdom a most wicked son, named Manasseh.

sentences.greek: Οὗτος γὰρ εἴδωλα ἐν τῷ ἁγιαστηρίῳ ἔστησε.
sentences.literal_english: This one for idols in the sanctuary stood.
sentences.smooth_english: For he set up idols in the sanctuary.

sentences.greek: Τότε ὁ Ναβουχοδονόσορ, ὁ τῆς Βαβυλῶνος βασιλεύς, πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τῆς γῆς διενοήσατο ὑφ᾿ ἑαυτῷ ποιεῖσθαι.
sentences.literal_english: Then the Nebuchadnezzar, the of the Babylon king, all the nations of the earth purposed under to himself to make.
sentences.smooth_english: Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, planned to bring all the nations of the earth under his rule.

sentences.greek: Τὸν μὲν Ὁλοφέρνην, τὸν ἀρχιστράτηγον τῆς δυνάμεως, ἐπὶ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἔπεμψεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand Holofernes, the chief-commander of the force, upon the Jews he sent.
sentences.smooth_english: He sent Holofernes, the commander of his army, against the Jews.

sentences.greek: Ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν ταῦτα οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ κατοικοῦντες, ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα, καὶ περὶ Ἱεροσολύμης καὶ περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ ἐταράχθησαν.
sentences.literal_english: As on the other hand heard these things the ones in the Judea dwelling, they feared exceedingly, and about Jerusalem and about the temple were troubled.
sentences.smooth_english: When those dwelling in Judea heard these things, they were greatly afraid, and there was turmoil concerning Jerusalem and the temple.

sentences.greek: Χήρα τις γυνή, τοὔνομα Ἰουδίθ, τοῦ Ὁλοφέρνου τὴν Βετυλούαν πολιορκήσαντος, τὴν πατρίδα αὐτῆς σῶσαι ἐπεχείρησεν.
sentences.literal_english: A widow certain woman, the name Judith, of the Holofernes the Bethulia having besieged, the fatherland of her to save attempted.
sentences.smooth_english: A certain widow, a woman named Judith, when Holofernes was besieging Bethulia, attempted to save her homeland.

sentences.greek: Ἐπεὶ οὖν τῷ Θεῷ προςηύξατο ἡ Ἰουδίθ, ἐξῆλθεν αὐτὴ ἐκ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἡ παιδίσκη αὐτῆς.

sentences.smooth_english: So after Judith prayed to God, she went out from the city, she and her maidservant.

sentences.greek: Οἱ δὲ δορυφόροι τοῦ στρατηγοῦ συνέλαβον αὐτήν, καὶ ἤγαγον ἐπὶ τὴν σκηνὴν Ὁλοφέρνου.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand bodyguards of the commander captured her, and led upon the tent of Holofernes.
sentences.smooth_english: The bodyguards of the general seized her and brought her to the tent of Holofernes.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν ἀρχιστράτηγος, τῇ ὄψει τῆς γυναικὸς ὑπαγόμενος, ἐβουλήθη συνδειπνεῖν μετ᾿ αὐτῆς, καὶ μεθυσθείς, εἰς ὕπνον καταφέρεται.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand chief-commander, to the sight of the woman being led under, wished to dine together with her, and having been made drunk, into sleep is carried down.
sentences.smooth_english: The commander-in-chief, overcome by the sight of the woman, wished to dine with her, and becoming drunk, fell asleep.

sentences.greek: Ἡ δὲ Ἰουδὶθ δακρύσασα, τῷ Θεῷ εἶπεν· Ὦ Κύριε, ἐπίῤῥωσόν με.
sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand Judith having wept, to the God said: O Lord, strengthen me.
sentences.smooth_english: But Judith, weeping, said to God, “O Lord, strengthen me.”

sentences.greek: Καὶ τότε λαβὼν τὸ ξίφος Ὁλοφέρνου, τὴν αὐτοῦ κεφαλὴν ἀπέταμεν.
sentences.literal_english: And then having taken the sword of Holofernes, the of him head cut off.
sentences.smooth_english: And then, taking the sword of Holofernes, she cut off his head.

sentences.greek: Ἣν γοῦν ἰδόντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, εἰς τοὺς Ἀσσυρίους προςώρμησαν, καὶ εἰς φυγὴν αὐτοὺς ἔτρεψαν.

sentences.smooth_english: When the Jews saw this, they rushed upon the Assyrians and put them to flight.

sentences.greek: Ἡ μὲν τοῦ Ἰούδα βασιλεία μέχρι νῦν ὑπῆρχεν· ἡ δὲ τῶν ἐσχάτων βασιλέων ἀσέβεια τὰ πράγματα κατέλυεν.
sentences.literal_english: The on the one hand of the Judah kingdom until now belonged; the on the other hand of the last kings impiety the affairs destroyed.
sentences.smooth_english: The kingdom of Judah existed until now; but the impiety of the last kings destroyed the state of affairs.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Ἰωαχὶμ βασιλεὺς εἰς τὸ πέρας τῶν ἀσεβημάτων ἀνέπεσε, καὶ τότε Ἱερεμίας, ὁ προφήτης, εἰςελθὼν εἰς τὸν ναόν, διὰ τῶν ἑορτασίμων ἡμερῶν, τὰ μέλλοντα ἔσεσθαι κακὰ προεφήτευσεν.
sentences.literal_english: The Jehoiakim king into the end of the impieties fell back, and then Jeremiah, the prophet, having entered into the temple, through of the festival days, the being about to be evils prophesied.
sentences.smooth_english: King Jehoiakim fell into the height of impieties, and then Jeremiah the prophet, entering the temple during the festival days, prophesied the evils that were to come.

sentences.greek: Οὐκοῦν ὁ Ναβουχοδονόσορ, ὁ δεύτερος, εἰςέβαλεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν, καί, πολιορκήσας τὴν Ἱεροσολύμην, ἐβεβήλωσε τὸν ναόν.

sentences.smooth_english: Therefore Nebuchadnezzar the second invaded Judea, and, besieging Jerusalem, defiled the temple.

sentences.greek: Ἠχμαλώτισε δὲ πολλοὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐν δὲ τοῖς Δανιήλ, Ἀνανίαν, Μισαήλ, καὶ Ἀζαρίαν.

sentences.smooth_english: He took many of the Jews captive, among them Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

sentences.greek: Ἐκ τούτου, ἤρξατο τὰ τῆς δουλείας ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτη.

sentences.smooth_english: From this began the seventy years of captivity.

sentences.greek: Τὸν δὲ Θεοῦ θυμὸν ἀνέφλεγεν ἔτι ἡ Ἱεροσολύμη, τοῦ Ἰεχωνίου βασιλεύοντος· τότε ὁ Ἰεζεχιήλ τε, καὶ ὁ Μαρδοχαῖος, καὶ ἄλλοι πολλοί, εἰς τὴν Βαβυλῶνα ᾐχμαλωτεύθησαν.

sentences.smooth_english: Yet Jerusalem further kindled the wrath of God while Jeconiah was king; then Ezekiel, and Mordecai, and many others were taken captive to Babylon.

sentences.greek: Ὁ μὲν δὴ Ναβουχοδονόσορ τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων βασιλείαν ἔδωκε τῷ Ματθανίᾳ, πατραδέλφῳ τοῦ Ἰεχωνίου, καὶ αὐτὸν ἐκάλεσε Σεδεκίαν.

sentences.greek: Τέλος δέ, ὑπὲρ τῶν συνεχῶν ἀποστάσεων τῆς Ἰουδαίας ὀργισθείς, τὴν Ἱεροσολύμην περιεκύκλωσεν.

sentences.greek: Ὁ λιμὸς τότε ἐνίσχυσεν ἐν τῇ πόλει.

sentences.smooth_english: Then famine grew strong in the city.

sentences.greek: Οἵ τε Χαλδαῖοι ἐπικατέλαβον τὸν Σεδεκίαν βασιλέα, οὗ τοὺς παῖδας ἔσφαξαν ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ.

sentences.smooth_english: The Chaldeans captured King Zedekiah, whose sons they slaughtered before him.

sentences.greek: Καὶ οὐ πολλῷ ὕστερον, ἦλθε μὲν Ναβουζαρδάν, ὁ τοῦ Ναβουχοδονόσορ στρατηγός, καὶ ἐνέπρησε τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Κυρίου, καὶ τὸ βασίλειον.

sentences.smooth_english: The people who were left in the city, he deported to Babylon.

sentences.greek: Οὐ μὴν ἀλλά, τῷ Ἱερεμίᾳ, ὃς τὴν τῆς Ἱεροσολύμης κατασκαφὴν προελελέχει, ὁ Ναβουχοδονόσορ ἐχρήσατο φιλικῶς.
sentences.literal_english: Not indeed but, to the Jeremiah, who the of the Jerusalem destruction had foretold, the Nebuchadnezzar used amicably.

sentences.greek: Καὶ τὸν Γοδολίαν κατέστησεν ἔπαρχον ἐπὶ πάντων ἀνθρώπων οὓς κατέλιπεν ἐν τῇ γῇ Ἰούδα.

sentences.smooth_english: And he appointed Gedaliah as governor over all the people he had left in the land of Judah.

sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand people, very fearfully having the Chaldeans, into the Egypt fled down.
sentences.smooth_english: But the people, fearing the Chaldeans, fled to Egypt.

sentences.greek: Ἐπειδὴ οὕτως ὅλην τὴν Ἰουδαίαν τῶν οἰκούντων χηρεύουσαν εἶδεν ὁ Ἱερεμίας, καὶ πάντα ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐρείπια, τοῦ Σιὼν μνημονεύων, ἐθρήνει οὕτως·
sentences.literal_english: Since thus whole the Judea of the ones dwelling being widowed saw the Jeremiah, and all in the city ruins, of the Zion remembering, he was lamenting thus:
sentences.smooth_english: When Jeremiah saw all Judea thus bereft of inhabitants, and everything in the city in ruins, remembering Zion, he lamented thus:

sentences.greek: Ἡ Ἱεροσολύμη, πεπληθυμμένη λαῶν, ὡς χήρα ἐγενήθη.

sentences.smooth_english: Jerusalem, once full of people, has become like a widow.

sentences.smooth_english: All the gates of Zion are destroyed, the priests sigh, the virgins are led away.

sentences.greek: Ἀκούσατε, λαοί, ἴδετε τὸ ἄλγος μου· ὁ Κύριος διέφθειρεν Ἰσραήλ. Σὺ δέ, ὦ Κύριε, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἔσῃ.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Δανιήλ, ὃς νεώτατος εἰς τὴν Βαβυλῶνος αἰχμαλωσίαν ἀπήχθη, μεγίστην νοῦ ἐνθέου ἀπόδειξιν παρέσχε.
sentences.literal_english: The Daniel, who youngest into the of Babylon captivity was led away, greatest of mind divine proof provided.
sentences.smooth_english: Daniel, who was taken as a youth into the Babylonian captivity, gave the greatest proof of inspired wisdom.

sentences.greek: Τὴν γὰρ Σωσάνναν ἀπέδειξεν ἀναίτιον εἶναι, ᾗ ἁγνοτάτῃ οὔσῃ δύο πρεσβῦται τοῦ λαοῦ αἰτίαν ψευδῆ ἐπήγαγον.
sentences.literal_english: The for Susanna he pointed out blameless to be, to whom most pure being two elders of the people charge false brought on.
sentences.smooth_english: For he proved Susanna to be innocent, against whom, though she was most pure, two elders of the people brought a false accusation.

sentences.greek: Οὐ πολλῷ ὕστερον, ὁ μὲν Ναβουχοδονόσορ, ὁ δεύτερος, ἐνύπνιον ἐνυπνιάσθη, καὶ ἐξέστη τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ· οἱ δὲ Χαλδαῖοι οὐκ ἔσχον τί εἴπωσιν αὐτῷ.
sentences.literal_english: Not much later, the on the one hand Nebuchadnezzar, the second, a dream dreamed, and stood out the spirit of him; the on the other hand Chaldeans not had what they might say to him.
sentences.smooth_english: Not long after, Nebuchadnezzar, the second, had a dream, and his spirit was troubled; but the Chaldeans had nothing to say to him.

sentences.smooth_english: Daniel stood before the king and interpreted his dream.

sentences.literal_english: The on the other hand king the Daniel and the three of him companions into great honors set down.
sentences.smooth_english: And the king placed Daniel and his three companions in great honor.

groups.group_title: 64. The youths are thrown into the furnace.

sentences.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ὁ Ναβουχοδονόσορ, διότι πολέμους εὐτυχῶς διεπολέμησε, τοὺς πάντας ἀρχομένους ἐκέλευσεν ἑαυτῷ προςκυνεῖν.
sentences.literal_english: And behold the Nebuchadnezzar, because wars successfully he warred through, the all being ruled he commanded to himself to worship.
sentences.smooth_english: And behold, Nebuchadnezzar, because he had waged wars successfully, ordered all his subjects to worship him.

sentences.greek: Μισαὴλ μέν, Ἀζαρίας, καὶ Ἀνανίας, οἱ τοῦ Δανιὴλ ἑταῖροι, οὐκ ἐθελήσαντες πείθεσθαι τῷ τοῦ Ναβουχοδονόσορ προςτάγματι, εἰς κάμινον φλεγομένην εἰςεβλήθησαν.
sentences.literal_english: Mishael on the one hand, Azariah, and Hananiah, the of the Daniel companions, not having wished to obey to the of Nebuchadnezzar command, into oven burning were cast in.
sentences.smooth_english: Mishael, Azariah, and Hananiah, Daniel’s companions, not wishing to obey Nebuchadnezzar’s command, were thrown into a burning furnace.

sentences.greek: Ἄγγελος δέ τις, συγκαταβὰς εἰς τὴν κάμινον, ἐξεῖρξεν αὐτοὺς τῆς φλογός.

sentences.smooth_english: But an angel, coming down into the furnace, drove them out of the flame.

sentences.greek: Τότε ὁ Ἀζαρίας, ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ πυρός, προςηύξατο· Εὐλογητὸς εἶ, ὦ Κύριε τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν.

sentences.smooth_english: Then Azariah, in the midst of the fire, prayed: Blessed are you, O Lord of our fathers.

sentences.greek: Ἀληθινὰ γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔργα σου, καὶ ὁδοί, καὶ κρίσεις.

sentences.greek: Ὁ Εὐϊαλμαρώδεκ τὸν Ναβουχοδονόσορ πατέρα διεδέξατο.
sentences.literal_english: The Evil-merodach the Nebuchadnezzar father succeeded.
sentences.smooth_english: Evil-merodach succeeded Nebuchadnezzar his father.

sentences.greek: Τοῦτον μὲν ὁ Δανιὴλ κατασκάπτειν τὸ εἴδωλον τοῦ Βὴλ παρήνεσεν. Ἔλεγε γάρ· Ὦ βασιλεῦ, μὴ σέβου εἴδωλα χειροποίητα, ἀλλὰ τὸν ζῶντα Θεόν, τὸν κτίσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
sentences.literal_english: This one on the one hand the Daniel to dig down the idol of the Bel exhorted. He was saying for: O king, not revere idols made by hand, but the living God, the having created the heaven and the earth.

sentences.greek: Μέγαν τε δράκοντα, ᾧ οἱ Βαβυλώνιοι προςεκύνουν, ἀνεῖλεν αὐτός.

sentences.greek: Ὁ δὲ λαὸς ὀργισθείς, παρὰ τοῦ βασιλέως ἔτυχε τοῦ ἐμβάλλεσθαι τὸν Δανιὴλ εἰς τὸν τῶν λεόντων λάκκον.

sentences.greek: Ἀλλὰ μεθ᾿ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας, ὁ προφήτης ἐκ τοῦ λάκκου σῶος ἐξεβλήθη.

sentences.greek: ἡ ἕκτη ἡμέρα.
sentences.literal_english: The sixth day.
sentences.smooth_english: The sixth day.

sentences.greek: ἡ γῆ ἐτελέσθη.
sentences.literal_english: The land was finished.
sentences.smooth_english: The land was finished.

sentences.greek: ὁ οὐρανὸς ἐτελέσθη.
sentences.literal_english: The sky was finished.
sentences.smooth_english: The sky was finished.

sentences.greek: πάντα ἐν τῇ γῇ καὶ τῷ οὐρανῷ ἐτελέσθη.
sentences.literal_english: Everything in the land and sky was finished.
sentences.smooth_english: Everything in the land and sky was finished.

sentences.greek: ὁ θεὸς ἀνεπαύσατο.
sentences.literal_english: God rested.
sentences.smooth_english: God rested.

sentences.greek: ἡ ἑβδόμη ἡμέρα ἁγία ἐστίν.
sentences.literal_english: The seventh day is holy.
sentences.smooth_english: The seventh day is holy.
